d8e130716c776d1d.title: Higher financing costs to weaken global credit conditions in 2027: Moody's
d8e130716c776d1d.summary: Moody's Ratings on Tuesday said it expects global credit conditions to weaken in 2027 due to higher financing costs and elevated energy prices. The Moody's Ratings' 2027 Global Credit Conditions Outlook report examines the key forces that could shape credit markets in the year ahead. It said AI investment will remain massive, but investors will increasingly focus on whether revenues and productivity gains justify the scale of spending. "Business model disruption will become more visible: some companies will gain from stronger demand and productivity, while others face more competition and weaker pricing power," Moody's Ratings said. Besides, Moody's expects government intervention through tariffs, regulation, export controls and strategic investment to play a growing role in credit outcomes. "As many of these tools can be introduced or reversed by executive action, policy can shift quickly, therefore this will continue to influence trade, capital allocation and competition in 2027

f7814ef3cf97c8de.title: FPIs turn net buyers in November, pump ₹53,739 crore into Indian equities
f7814ef3cf97c8de.summary: Foreign investors turned net buyers of Indian equities in November, infusing Rs 53,739 crore in the first nine days after two consecutive months of outflows, driven by the AI-led sell-off in global markets, strong domestic earnings growth and attractive large-cap valuations. The latest investment follows net outflows of Rs 34,843 crore in October and Rs 35,861 crore in September, according to data available with the depositories. "The sudden change in FPI stance was triggered by the AI sell-off in the US and other AI markets like South Korea, Taiwan and Japan. "This sell-off, in turn, was triggered by fears surrounding data centre spending in the US. The Democrats, who won both chambers of Congress, are opposed to indiscriminate data centre spending. They will demand guardrails for AI," said V K Vijayakumar, Chief Investment Strategist at Geojit Investments. The AI-led sell-off has made India, widely regarded as a non-AI trade, an attractive destination for Foreign Portfolio Invest

690b1d8a6ade612c.summary: Mahindra Group Chairman Anand Mahindra on Tuesday said India is not just a refuge from the AI hype but rather has "a compelling AI opportunity of its own". In a post on X, Mahindra cited the nation's software talent, systems integration expertise and enormous domestic market for AI use cases, to make his point: "surely India has a promising hand to play?" "Perhaps India isn't just a refuge from the AI hype. It may have a compelling AI opportunity of its own," he wrote. And if so, he argued, the renewed interest in Indian equities "may have more staying power than we think". In his post, Mahindra said he had earlier flagged the irony of India returning to favour with global investors partly because it was seen as being outside the supposedly overheated AI trade. "But perhaps there's another way to look at it," he said. He pointed out that Stanford now ranks India third in global AI vibrancy. Mahindra acknowledged that India does not make the most advanced chips or lead the race i

774c708eded497ec.summary: Transactions through the popular Unified Payments Interface (UPI) witnessed a 32 per cent surge in volume terms on Diwali driven by last-minute festival buying. UPI volume increased to 916.9 million on November 8 from 695.7 million transactions on the same day last year, according to data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI). In value terms, UPI transactions rose to Rs 90,029.43 crore on November 8 against Rs 88,350.79 crore last year. A day prior to Diwali, the transaction volume was 975.8 million resulting in transfer of Rs 1,36,118 crore. UPI is an instant payment system developed by the NPCI. NPCI, an initiative of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) and the Indian Banks' Association (IBA), is an umbrella organisation for operating retail payments and settlement systems in India. A total of 3,79,980 candidates will appear for the two examinations. The ICSE (class 10) examination will see 2.70 lakh candidates from 3,106 affiliated schools, while more than 1.1 lakh candidates from 1,651 schools will appear for the ISC (class 12) examination. The ICSE examination will cover 76 subjects or papers, while the ISC examination will feature 60 subjects. "The ICSE year 2027 examination will commence on February 15, 2027, and conclude on March 31, 2027. The examination will be conducted across 2,835 examination centres in India and overseas. Taking note of the government’s submission, Justice Amit Mahajan said no interim directions were necessary at this stage. The court, however, permitted the club to remove its belongings from the premises within a week. “Considering the above, no order is required to be passed. The club, earlier known as Talkatora Club, has challenged the government’s decision to withdraw its recognition as well as an eviction order issued by the estate officer directing it to immediately vacate its premises in the President’s Estate. The interim relief was sought against the July 14, 2026 de-recognition order and the July 17, 2026 eviction order. During the November 5 hearing, the Centre’s counsel informed the court that there was no proposal to allot the premises to any party at present. According to the club, the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) arbitrarily, illegally and unconstitutionally withdrew its recognition on July 14. The petitioner said that instead of taking corrective action on its complaints regarding irregularities during the term of the ad hoc committee managing its affairs, the authorities first withdrew the recognition in February without issuing any show cause notice. It said it would not accede to the request. The Bench was constituted in September and has heard the matter four times since September 18, 2026. It has heard submissions from advocate Arvind Datar for a petitioner who challenges the quota. It is hearing petitioners. The legislature passed the Act on February 20, 2024, and it was subsequently notified on February 26, 2024. The Act rests on a report of the commission under Justice Sunil Shukre. 04b9e8c6ff989ba3.title: Karnataka-registered doctors may be allowed to practise in Kasaragod: Keralam Health Minister
04b9e8c6ff989ba3.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:04 am IST - KASARAGOD Keralam Health Minister K. Muraleedharan The Keralam government has recommended to the State Medical Council that doctors registered with the Karnataka Medical Council be allowed to practise in Kasaragod, considering the district’s special circumstances, Health Minister K. Muraleedharan has said. The medical council is expected to take a favourable decision on the recommendation soon, the Minister said while inaugurating ‘Kayakalpam’, a public outreach programme of the Health Minister. Government hospitals should have adequate number of doctors, nurses, pharmacists, and laboratory technicians, the Minister said, adding that additional posts had been sought. Their early sanction would considerably ease staff shortage in the district. The extension of the tenure of National Health Mission employees in Kasaragod till March 31 was also an indication of the government’s commitment to the district, he said. The Minister said that he would direct the authorities to convene a meeting of the Endosulfan cell soon. Periye in Kasaragod was among the four locations proposed by the government to the Centre for setting up an All India Institute of Medical Sciences, he said. Instructions had been issued to make hostel facilities available at the Kasaragod Medical College within two months. The construction of a hostel for nursing students would begin within three months, he added. The government would ensure the services of a forensic surgeon at the Kanhangad district hospital. A new building for the District Medical Office would be constructed at a cost of ₹4.8 crore. 5f1fb05fb2789013.summary: The Election Commission on Tuesday said restrictions and prohibitions applicable to serving government employees under the Model Code of Conduct (MCC) will also apply to retired government officials and other individuals engaged by state and Union territory governments. A joint action council has been formed, and hundreds of residents have joined the agitation against the outlets and the Mahe administration, demanding the immediate intervention of the authorities in the matter. Later, there was a smell resembling soap and now petrol or diesel,” he said. According to Mr. Premraj, samples collected from six wells near three petrol pumps tested positive for petroleum hydrocarbon. c65d287d2023421b.summary: This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. New Delhi: After India's gram (chana) imports fell in FY26 from a record high a year earlier, the government is stepping up efforts to strengthen domestic production of the pulse and further reduce import dependence and keep prices under control. The Department of Consumer Affairs is identifying rainfed areas that can be brought under chana cultivation, two people aware of the matter said. It has identified 80 districts across states, including Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat, Haryana, Punjab, Jharkhand and Bihar, where rainfed land could be utilised to grow the crop, the people said. India imported gram worth $3.63 billion in FY26, down from a record $5.54 billion in FY25. The proposed move aims to build on this reduction by expanding domestic chana supplies. “The government has a tentative estimate of around 2.38 million hectares of rainfed land across watershed areas in the identified states, and the exact extent of land suitable for chana cultivation will be mapped by the two departments,” said the first among the two officials cited above. "As part of the plan, the department will approach the agriculture ministry and the Department of Land Resources to identify suitable acreage and assess its additional production potential,” the official added. The department plans to support farmers with quality seeds and technical assistance, along with procurement assurance, the second official said. Chana is a relatively less water-intensive crop that can be grown using residual soil moisture after the kharif harvest. The government expects the proposed expansion to strengthen domestic supplies and eventually create scope for chana dal exports, subject to domestic demand and surplus availability. 2c176b9bf28da1a6.title: State govt. employees who donate organs likely to get leave for recuperation
2c176b9bf28da1a6.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:15 am IST - CHENNAI Health Minister K.G. Arunraj speaking at an event organised by Gleneagles Hospital in Chennai on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: J. Johan Sathyadas Health Minister K.G. Arunraj on Tuesday said that the State government was likely to provide 42 days of leave to employees who donate organs. Similarly, if organ donors themselves need organs, their needs will be prioritised. Speaking at an event to honour over 250 living donor liver transplantation journeys, supported by the Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme at Gleneagles Hospital, he said that government hospitals too will soon take up live liver organ transplants in a transparent manner. Dr. Arunraj urged the public to take care of their liver health. He said that those who are used to consuming alcohol every day should gradually reduce the quantum and take to responsible drinking. A. Aravind, Director of Medical Education, said that the cost of one live liver transplant was around ₹22 lakh and it was great that the State government was making it possible through insurance. Joy Varghese, director of Hepatology, Gleneagles, said that over 100 beneficiaries of live liver transplant were children between the ages of 5 and 14. Many of them had been referred from the government-run hospitals, he said, adding that the hospital was indebted to doctors in government hospitals for the trust they placed in them. Sholinganallur MLA P. Saravanan, S. Niranjani, chief operating officer, and J. Sophia Ansetta, medical director were present. 4459a04203b498ad.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:34 am IST - NEW DELHI Indian women’s hockey goalkeeper Savita Punia. File | Photo Credit: PTI Veteran goalkeeper Savita Punia has been rested from the Asian Champions Trophy in Bhopal, replaced by Bansari Solanki in the Indian women's hockey squad unveiled on Tuesday, with head coach Sjoerd Marijne also announcing changes to the roles of some players during the event. The tournament is scheduled to be held from November 19 to 28 at the newly-built International Sports Complex, Nathu Barkheda, Bhopal and India will enter as the defending champions. India will begin their campaign against Malaysia on the opening day of the competition. Mid-fielder Salima Tete will continue to lead the team, which is playing its first international tournament after the historic gold medal at the Asian Games in Japan last month. The hosts have secured the ACT title in 2016, 2023 and 2024. The six-team competition will feature India, China, Japan, Malaysia, Thailand and South Korea. Like India, South Korea too have won the Women’s Asian Champions Trophy three times. The 25-year-old Bansari has been part of the squad that won the Asia Cup last year. Bichu Devi Kharibam retained her place as the other custodian in the squad. "This is the moment I want to give other players the chance to showcase their talent on the international stage. Some players will be playing in different positions than they normally do, so that I can see how they perform in a different role," said Marijne. "We are excited to play in front of the home crowd and finish the year well," he added. As part of the role shuffling, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal, who played as a forward in the Asian Games, has been named in the mid-field for the ACT. Similarly, mid-fielder Nikki Pradhan is part of the defensive line-up, while Ishika Chaudhary has been moved from defence to mid-field. f48a08324b837576.title: A hundred years ago | A case under the Companies Act
f48a08324b837576.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:26 am IST Bombay, November 10: Mr. P.D. Shamdasani, a shareholder of the Tata Iron and Steel Company and a most persistent critic of the Tata House, has for once succeeded in putting seven of the Steel Company’s Directors in the wrong though he has in almost every shareholders’ meeting of the company threatened them with prosecution on many allegations of mismanagement. The present case against Sri Dorab Tata, Sir Cowasji Jehangir, Narottam Morarji, Sir Phiroze Sethna, Mr. N.B. Saklatwala, Mr. F.E. Dinshaw and Sir Ibrahim Rabintulla Tata Sons Ltd and others is that they failed to comply with the provisions of the Indian Companies Act in not having convened the Company’s annual general meeting within fifteen months of the preceding meeting. The accused, in pleading guilty, urged that this was a fit case for warning and discharge. The Magistrate expressed inability to do so as this was a case under the Indian Companies Act and not one under the Penal Code. He convicted and fined them to a pay a fine of Rs. 5 each. cca4b5e6e501b12d.title: Kin of three workers who died at private firm in Hosur agree to receive bodies
cca4b5e6e501b12d.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 12:37 am IST - SALEM A day after three men allegedly died of asphyxiation on the premises of Tata Marigold Company (a unit of Tata Electronics) in Hosur, their relatives agreed to receive their bodies on Tuesday. Acknowledging the tragedy, Nalco Water, in a statement, said: “We are deeply saddened by the tragic incident that resulted in the deaths of three workers engaged by a sub-contractor of Nalco Water, an Ecolab company, at the Tata Electronics site. This incident occurred in a utility facility, operated by Nalco Water. We are working with the local authorities in the investigation of this incident.” On Monday evening, contract workers B. Akmal, 28, of Panchapalli and M. Sarathi Kumar, 28, of Thirumalvadi in Dharmapuri district; and Kaveri, 30, of Hosur in Krishnagiri district had carried out maintenance and cleaning work inside the nano-filtration feed tank at the factory in Vanniyapuram. At the time, the three experienced difficulty breathing and collapsed. They were rushed to a private hospital but died on the way. On Tuesday, relatives of the deceased tried to stage a road roko outside the Krishnagiri Government Medical College Hospital, where the three bodies were being kept, to demand compensation for the deaths. The police restrained them. Subsequently, the sub-contractor conducted talks with the relatives in the presence of District Superintendent of Police G.S. Anitha and assured them a solatium of ₹30 lakh each apart from the insurance amount. Based on the assurance, the relative agreed to receive the bodies after a post-mortem. Nalco Water said, “Our first priority is to extend all possible support to the families. Safety is a core value and is fundamental to everything we do at Ecolab. We take this incident extremely seriously. We are deeply committed to upholding the highest standards of safety across our operations and the sites where we work.” Published - November 11, 2026 12:37 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutio

73c1d076fc4d4ad0.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:52 pm IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Dr Rupali Basu, senior vice president, regional business head - East and Andhra Pradesh, HCG Cancer Centre, during an interaction with The Hindu in Visakhapatnam on Tuesday. | Photo Credit: V RAJU Early diagnosis of cancer, coupled with timely intervention and access to appropriate treatment, is crucial to improving survival rates and in helping patients lead a better quality of life, said Rupali Basu, senior vice president, regional business head - East and Andhra Pradesh, HCG Cancer Centre. Emphasising the need to strengthen cancer awareness and screening, Ms. Basu said that many patients continued to approach hospitals only at an advanced stage of the disease owing to fear, social stigma, lack of awareness of early symptoms, financial concerns and geographical barriers to accessing specialised healthcare. Stronger community-level awareness programmes and accessible screening facilities could play a significant role in changing this trend, she said. Speaking to The Hindu , she said that cancer was increasingly emerging as a concern across age groups and communities, with several factors, including an ageing population, tobacco consumption, cigarette smoking, changing lifestyles and environmental exposure, contributing to the growing burden. While breast cancer remained a major concern among women, lung and colorectal cancers were among the commonly diagnosed cancers in men. Brain tumours and other forms of cancer also required greater awareness and timely medical attention. Ms. Basu stressed that cancer treatment required more than just identifying the disease. A multidisciplinary approach, involving tumour boards, was essential to determine the most appropriate course of treatment for each patient. Accurate diagnosis, the latest medical technology and coordinated care could make a significant difference to treatment outcomes and the patient’s overall experience. 32e378b7558b4e37.title: The War Putin Wanted to Keep Away Is Coming Home to Russia
32e378b7558b4e37.summary: Olga was jolted awake by an explosion so powerful that her apartment building shuddered and the windows and furniture shook. Looking outside, she saw a plume of thick black smoke rising from a military equipment factory that had just been hit by a missile. Residents panicked, said Olga, a 49-year-old choreographer. “We didn’t know whether we should run to a shelter,” she said. The strike on the plant left six people dead and another 26 injured, according to the local governor. Olga doesn’t live in Kyiv, Kherson or any other Ukrainian city that’s been pounded for years by President Vladimir Putin’s forces. This is Kirov, a Russian city about 800 kilometers northeast of Moscow known for its 16th century onion-domed monastery rather than being in a war zone. The missile strike was one of the many that have inflicted rising civilian casualties inside Russia in recent months. They are bringing Putin’s war home to his own people after he promised a swift and glorious victory. Since Ukrainian strikes intensified in mid-summer, people inside Russia are killed almost every week, according to a Bloomberg analysis of statements from regional authorities on their Telegram channels. Meanwhile, as Russia prepared to resume trilateral negotiations with the US and Ukraine on a potential peace deal in Abu Dhabi this week, confidential data hacked from Russia’s statistics service showed about 400,000 of its people have been killed fighting in Ukraine. It’s a scale of military deaths the country hasn’t seen since World War II. The Kremlin tightly controls the narrative around the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, now nine months into its fifth year. While the death toll touches a huge number of families in Russia, it won’t necessarily have political consequences for Putin, who taps into historical memory to justify the sacrifice in what he claims is an existential fight with the West in Ukraine. ee4a7dd1e82b3913.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 05:30 am IST - New Delhi Delhi’s air quality improved to the ‘poor’ category on Tuesday, with the 24-hour average AQI recorded at 299, just below the ‘very poor’ threshold of 300. | Photo Credit: ANI The Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) on Tuesday indicated that it was considering steps to capture peak levels of particulate matter (PM), a major pollutant, that exceed the existing monitoring range, after air quality data from several government monitoring stations in Delhi went missing for hours during the pollution spike following Deepavali on Sunday. The Hindu reported on Monday that the data gaps had led to an artificially lower official air quality index (AQI), making air quality appear better than it actually was, according to experts. In a statement on Tuesday, the CPCB said PM levels were measured only up to 1,000 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³) for AQI calculations, which explained the missing data on Deepavali night, when actual concentrations exceeded this limit. “The PM analysers deployed at the time of introduction of the NAQI (National Air Quality Index) [in 2015] were calibrated for a measurement range of 0-1,000 µg/m³. Accordingly, consistent with this, the designed system of automated data validation treats hourly readings beyond the calibrated range as outside range, and such readings are not used in the computation,” the CPCB statement read. “During extreme episodes, which are occasional, like Diwali firecracker bursting, this may appear as a data gap at the particular station concerned, and those hours do not contribute to the 24-hour average of the relevant pollutant for the concerned station,” the statement added. The CPCB said internal deliberations and consultations on processing data “beyond system design range” were under way. 259f3a995c68bcd1.title: Tasmac introduces three year transfer norm for shop employees
259f3a995c68bcd1.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 12:15 am IST - Chennai Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. (File) | Photo Credit: B. VELANKANNI RAJ The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation (Tasmac) is set to reshuffle employees across its retail network in Tamil Nadu, deploying staff at outlets based on manpower requirements. Under a new Transfer and Posting Policy for Tasmac liquor Retail Vending Shop Personnel, 2026, the state run liquor retailer has proposed transferring employees across shops once every three years. This is aimed at streamlining staff deployment and addressing manpower shortages. This one time rationalisation will be completed by November 30, 2026. The policy will apply to Supervisor (Shop-In-Charge), Salesman and Assistant Salesman. Exceptions will be given to shop personnel who are differently-abled or any genuine administrative circumstances. Tasmac headquarters will classify every shop as an A, B and C shop on the basis of its average daily sales and accordingly deploy workforce. Outlets with average monthly sales of ₹10 lakh and above will be classified as Category A and will have a minimum workforce of nine employees. Those with sales of more than ₹5 lakh but less than ₹10 lakh will fall under Category B, with a workforce of eight employees. Outlets recording sales of less than ₹5 lakh will be classified as Category C and will have five employees. The minimum number of manpower will vary based on operational requirements. Also, the classification of shops will be done every year based on the sales performance of each outlet, according to official sources. Employees who have complete three years at a shop as on November 1 will be considered for the transfer. It also directed them to file responses on measures presently in place to identify, monitor and regulate vehicles that do not conform to the prescribed emission standards, including the enforcement of Pollution Under Control (PUC) certification requirements. 75e338a3dfe88607.title: India A-New Zealand A series ends in draw after rain washes out fourth day of third unofficial Test
75e338a3dfe88607.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 01:14 am IST - LINCOLN, NEW ZEALAND The third and final unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A ended in a draw, with the series ending in a draw. All three four-day matches failed to produce a result. At the end of day 4, NZ A was 36/2, with Dean Foxcroft (10*) and Zak Gibson (1*) unbeaten. They trailed by 428 runs. Earlier, New Zealand A won the toss and elected to field first. A 175-run opening stand between Yashasvi Jaiswal (102 in 138 balls, with 16 fours and two sixes) and Sai Sudharsan (88 in 215 balls, with 11 fours) started off things for India. Half-centuries came from the bat of Tilak Varma (81 in 164 balls, with five fours and two sixes), skipper Dhruv Jurel (71 in 95 balls, with nine fours and two sixes) and Washington Sundar (50* in 107 balls, with two fours) as India posted 464/5. Zak Gibson (2/73) was the leading wicket-taker for NZ. India’s batting was a big plus ahead of the Test series starting on November 19, with Devdutt Padikkal (326 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 65.20, with a century and a fifty) being the top run-scorer. After a few poor scores, Yashasvi Jaiswal (279 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 69.75, with two centuries) also scored back-to-back tons. Sai Sudharsan (231 runs in three matches and five innings at an average of 46.20, with two fifties) and skipper Jurel (179 runs in three matches and four innings at an average of 44.75, with a century and a fifty) also played some fine knocks for India. Uncapped batter Yash Rathod (223 runs in two matches at an average of 111.50, with a century and a fifty) also was a big positive for India. Auqib Nabi (six wickets in a match) and Mohammed Siraj (four wickets in a match) were the leading wicket-takers for India. India Test squad for two NZ Tests: Shubman Gill [C], Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul [VC], Devdutt Padikkal, Rishabh Pant [WK]*, Dhruv Jurel [WK], Ravindra Jadeja, Anshul Kamboj, Jasprit Bumrah, Pras

253bffb21fcd20e3.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:34 pm IST - KANNUR A 56-year-old woman and her 21-year-old son died on Tuesday (November 10) after they were found with serious wounds at their home in Mattannur. The deceased were identified as Jyothi and Naveen Krishna. Jyothi’s husband, Jayakrishnan, reportedly found them lying in a pool of blood on the second floor of their house on Lions Club Road when he returned home after visiting Mattannur town around 9.30 a.m. The police and residents rushed to the house and took the two to the hospital. The police said both were in an extremely critical condition on the way to the hospital. The Mattannur police have registered a case and stepped up the investigation. db5df5e4f7a3cce5.title: Around 150 persons treated for cracker-related burns in Vellore, nearby districts
db5df5e4f7a3cce5.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:55 pm IST - VELLORE Sanitary workers remove cracker wastes in Vellore Corporation. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement Around 150 persons received treatment for cracker-related burns at various healthcare centres, government hospitals in Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts. Health officials said that the Government Medical College and Hospital in Vellore and Tiruvannamalai treated 22 and 35 persons respectively for cracker-related burns. “Most of the victims were treated as out-patients. They were below the age of 15. A team of health officials was deployed for the purpose,” said Edvina Vasantha, dean, Government Medical College Hospital in Tiruvannamalai. In Tirupattur district, on an average, 10-12 cases of burns were reported at the Government Taluk Hospital at Tirupattur, Vaniyambadi, Ambur, and Natrampalli towns each, during the festival. The government health centres in Jawadhu Hills also reported at least 15 burn cases over three days (November 7-9). “No major burns were reported within Vellore town during the festival. Adequate medical teams were in place to attend to emergencies,” P. Pratap Kumar, City Health Officer (CHO), Vellore Corporation, told The Hindu . In Ranipet district, more than 40 cases of burns were reported in government hospitals at Arakkonam, Walajah, Arcot, Ranipet, and Sholinghur towns during the festival. Health officials said that private hospitals and clinics also reported cases of cracker-related burns. Most of the persons are treated as out-patients in these districts. A large volume of cracker waste was generated in these districts. Around 550 tonnes of cracker wastes were generated in Vellore and Tiruvannamalai Corporation on November 8-9. More than 500 sanitary workers were roped in for the purpose. Most of the wastes include paper, cardboard, half-burnt, and unused crackers that are mostly dumped on roads and streets. These were sent to micro compost centres for recycling.

fe2151dac5c26ccb.title: No plans to switch federations as of now: Abhimanyu
fe2151dac5c26ccb.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 11:55 pm IST - Budapest Abhimanya Mishra. | Photo Credit: File photo: SUDHAKARA JAIN American Grandmaster Abhimanyu Mishra said he has no current plans to switch federations, explaining that his earlier comments referred to a hypothetical situation. “Actually, this was a huge miscommunication. Essentially, as of now, I don’t want to switch federations at all,” Abhimanyu told The Hindu on the sidelines of the Total Chess World Championship Tour pilot here. He said his response to that hypothetical question was that he might consider a switch. “But the thing is, this does not mean that I’m searching to change federation at all currently,” he said. Abhimanyu also spoke about playing simultaneous exhibitions to help cover expenses. The sessions, which involved taking on several opponents and could last hours, provided some income but were tiring. “And I was getting some money out of that, which was helping a bit,” he said. In Budapest, Abhimanyu has been drawn in Group C alongside Magnus Carlsen, Anish Giri, Ian Nepomniachtchi, Haik M. Martirosyan and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov. He will face each opponent twice in the Fast Classic group stage. The 24-player event combines blitz, rapid and Fast Classic, with players tested at all three speeds in the knockouts. The chance to play Carlsen twice was particularly appealing, with Abhimanyu describing it as a source of joy and a learning experience. TThe strength of the field had convinced him to accept the invitation. “I mean, saying no to a tournament like this is a bit ridiculous, honestly,” he said. bcef827141be2997.title: Two persons killed in separate road incidents
bcef827141be2997.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 11:48 pm IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Two persons were killed in separate road incidents near Kilpennathur and Arcot towns in Tiruvannamalai and Ranipet districts respectively on Tuesday. The police identified the victims as V. Nandakumar, 45, and T. Venkatesan, 35. Initial inquiry revealed that Nandakumar, a private school staff, was on his way to school on the Chennai – Bengaluru Highway (NH 48) when a private bus hit the two-wheeler he was riding at Melvisharam in Ranipet. Passersby rushed a badly injured Nandakumar to Government Taluk Hospital in Arcot town, where doctors said that he was brought dead. A case was registered and a probe is under way. In a separate incident, the victim, Venkatesan was riding his autorickshaw from a petrol pump towards the Chittoor – Cuddalore Highway at Kilpennathur, when a car rammed the autorickshaw. The police said in the impact, Venkatesan died on the spot. On being informed, Kilpennathur police inspected the spot and a case was registered. Special teams were formed to nab the car driver, and a probe is under way. 65337055769d5a1d.title: Fifty years ago | Foreign intelligence agents at work in U.S.
65337055769d5a1d.summary: Published - November 11, 2026 02:44 am IST Washington, November 10: Either with or without the knowledge of the U.S. Government, a number of foreign intelligence organisations appear to have established a regular presence in the United States, and have been engaged in activities which are for the most part illegal. The most publicised case to-date is that of the South Korean Intelligence Agency (KCIA), which has been accused of not only spying on South Korean and American nationals in the U.S., but also of giving huge bribes to U.S. Congressmen and others in a bid to influence U.S. defence and foreign policies — former Defence Secretary Melvin Laird has now disclosed that in 1970 the South Korean “lobby” tried to undermine the Nixon Administration’s decision to withdraw 20,000 American troops from South Korea. 668f2c96f4be6283.title: Russia-Ukraine-US talks: Key milestones in peace negotiations since 2022
668f2c96f4be6283.summary: Negotiators from Russia, Ukraine and the US are to meet Tuesday and Wednesday in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, in the latest bid to end the war. Key developments from past sessions since Moscow's full-scale invasion of its neighbor on Feb. 24, 2022: Feb. 28, 2022: Ukrainian and Russian delegations meet in neighboring Belarus for the first time after the invasion. Talks continue for two weeks, deciding only on humanitarian corridors for evacuating civilians. March 10, 2022: Russian and Ukrainian Foreign Ministers Sergey Lavrov and Dmytro Kuleba meet in Antalya, Turkiye. March 21, 2022: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy calls for direct talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin, an idea rebuffed by Lavrov. March 28-30, 2022: Delegations meet in Istanbul to work on a draft peace agreement. Moscow says it's willing to "fundamentally cut back" military activity near Kyiv and the northern city of Chernihiv; Ukraine says it's open to discussing neutral status for Ukraine if it

The Trump administration last year pulled the US out of the Human Rights Council, accusing it of an anti-US and anti-Israel bias, and alleging that it didn't uphold the very values it promotes. Supporters back the council's mandate to keep tabs on human rights in all UN member states including the US, which has drawn criticism for its policies including strong-arm deportations and targeted killings of alleged drug-runners in the Caribbean and Pacific - which the administration has said are designed to protect US workers and help keep the country safe. 4f4a1af698b44ae6.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
4f4a1af698b44ae6.summary: Updated - November 11, 2026 01:13 am IST If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues. In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. d83b333384396245.title: IND vs NZ 3rd ODI abandoned due to rain, India retains 2-0 series lead
d83b333384396245.summary: Rain played spoilsport as the third ODI between New Zealand and India at Seddon Park here on Tuesday was called off. India lead the five-match series 2-0 as the two teams head to Tauranga for the final two games, scheduled for November 13 and 15. India skipper Shubman Gill won the toss for the third time in a row and opted to bowl, fielding an unchanged side from the previous two games. However, just as the covers were coming off for a 40-overs-a-side contest, the heavens opened up once again. With at least 70 minutes remaining before the local cut-off time of 7:50 pm for a 20-overs-a-side game, the two umpires decided to call off the match. The weather forecast for this game had always been gloomy, with a 90 per cent chance of rain predicted throughout the day. This was supposed to be the last game of the series for skipper Shubman Gill and senior wicketkeeper KL Rahul before they link up with the Test squad in Wellington. They will be accompanied by Kuldeep Yadav, Anshul Kamboj

7f3ebff4cc6a832e.title: Five persons, including four girls, drown in irrigation tank in Tiruvannamalai
7f3ebff4cc6a832e.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:20 am IST - TIRUVANNAMALAI Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar during their inspection of the irrigation tank on Monday. | Photo Credit: Special arrangement A staff nurse and four girls of a government-recognised children’s home for girls drowned in an irrigation tank at Samuthiram village here on Monday (November 9, 2026). The deceased were identified as staff nurse Thenmozhi, 24, Vijayalakshmi, 14, Alli, 14, Poomika, 13, and Valliammal, 16. Except Valliammal, who belongs to Kilpennathur village, the other three girls are siblings from Karapattu village near Chengam. The deceased did not know swimming, the police said. Initial inquiry revealed the home had been functioning for over a decade in the area. On Monday afternoon, Thenmozhi, along with around 13 girls, went to the irrigation tank on Perumbakkam Main Road to bathe. Poomika and her siblings and Valliammal stepped into the water and slipped and fell into a deeper portion of the irrigation tank. The police said Thenmozhi tried to save the children but also drowned. Hearing the other girls’ shouts, the area’s residents rushed to the spot and alerted the Tiruvannamalai West police and firefighters. Firefighters retrieved the bodies and sent them to the Government Medical College and Hospital in Tiruvannamalai town for a post-mortem. A case has been registered. Collector Vandhana Garg and Superintendent of Police R. Uthayakumar met the families of the deceased at the hospital in the presence of hospital dean Edvina Vasantah and inspected the irrigation tank. A probe is under way. 12f72c3e816cf159.title: WTA Chennai Open: Postponement of singles final sparks controversy
12f72c3e816cf159.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:11 am IST - CHENNAI The postponement of the WTA 250 Chennai Open singles final due to rain and fireworks-induced smog on Sunday evening sparked controversy over the organisers’ handling of the situation. The final, set for a 6:30 p.m. start, was delayed thrice due to rain. Once the rain relented for good, the organisers dried the centre court at the SDAT stadium and rescheduled the final at 9 p.m. However, the smog caused by the Deepavali firecrackers had made the air quality hazardous and the match had to be shifted to 11 a.m. on Monday in which Poland’s Magda Linette defeated Indonesia’s Janice Tjen, the reigning champion, in three sets. Christopher Bint, Tjen’s coach, in an Instagram story late on Sunday night, claimed that the organisers wanted to conduct the final despite the extremely poor air quality. “And they still wanted the match to go ahead,” he wrote, attaching a screenshot showing an AQI of 1556 in Chennai. Later, after Monday’s summit clash, Bint said, “Maybe, it could have just been postponed a little bit earlier.” Linette felt the doubles final, which started at 4 p.m. on Sunday, could have been moved forward. “We should have put the doubles final way earlier which would have given us a lot of time,” said the 34-year-old Pole. Hiten Joshi, the tournament director, said, “In these emergencies, the tournament supervisor (Sheetal Iyer) has to get permission from the WTA. So, they were going back and forth, and she also wanted to wait to see if any play was possible.” Published - November 10, 2026 12:11 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. 40a90eb64af97d91.title: APSDRF rescues eight, evacuates 341 during Cyclone Arnab relief efforts
40a90eb64af97d91.summary: Updated - November 10, 2026 12:20 am IST - VIJAYAWADA DGP Harish Kumar Gupta presenting rewards to the APSDRF personnel at the AP Police Headquarters in Mangalagiri on Monday. | Photo Credit: BY ARRANGEMENT The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Response Force (APSDRF) shifted 341 people to safe places, rescued eight, and retrieved a body during Cyclone Arnab. Inspector General of Police (IGP-Operations) Ch. Srikanth, along with senior officers of Andhra Pradesh Special Police (APSP) met Director General of Police (DGP) Harish Kumar Gupta at the Police Headquarters at Mangalagiri on Monday (November 9, 2026), and explained the operations taken up by APSDRF during the calamity. The SDRF officials explained that eleven special teams comprising 328 officers and personnel rendered services in the State from October 27 to November 1. Rescue and relief operations were carried out in Bapatla, Konaseema, Kakinada, Srikakulam, Alluri Sitharama Raju, West Godavari, East Godavari, Polavaram, and Anakapalli districts. A total of 728 fallen trees were cleared, road clearance operations were taken up at 58 locations, and 31 electricity poles that fell on roads were removed, facilitating the movement of emergency vehicles, Mr. Srikanth said. The ‘Dial 112’ State Control Room played a crucial role in providing assistance to the people trapped in cyclone. In three days, the control room staff received 369 cyclone-related emergency calls from 17 districts. fc50fb31451033a0.title: Diwali 2026: Global leaders – Anthony Albanese, Emmanuel Macron, Mark Carney – call for unity, peace, prosperity
fc50fb31451033a0.summary: Wishing peace, prosperity, and hope, world leaders—including Emmanuel Macron, Anthony Albanese, and Mark Carney—shared their Diwali greetings on Sunday with all those celebrating the festival of lights. Albanese said Diwali was “the great celebration of the victory of light,” bringing communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. “We can all take pride and joy in just how intrinsically Diwali has become part of the face of modern Australia,” he said in a video message, noting that the signs and symbols of Diwali carry a message that speaks beyond religion or culture. Anthony Albanese, Emmanuel Macron and Mark Carney were among the leaders who sent greetings. Messages also came from leaders in Sri Lanka, the UAE, Pakistan, Israel, Malaysia and the Seychelles. Albanese described Diwali as a celebration of light that brings communities together across religious and cultural boundaries. He said its message calls for compassion, understanding, love and unity. Macron wished people unity, peace and hope, while Carney highlighted Diwali’s symbolism: light over darkness, good over evil and knowledge over ignorance. In Bangkok, Thailand’s prime minister inaugurated the Amazing Thailand Grand Diwali Festival, a 27-day event. In the United States, Donald Trump marked the occasion by lighting a diya at the White House. Gautam Gambhir, Jay Shah, the BCCI, former cricketers and IPL teams shared festive messages. Their wishes emphasized peace, prosperity, family, togetherness and hope. “It is a call to compassion and understanding, and of love and unity,” he said. “Wishing all my Indian friends in India, France, and around the world, a very happy Diwali! May its light inspire us to ever uphold unity, peace, and hope!” Macron wrote on social media, alongside a similar message in Hindi. Carney said communities across Canada were joining millions around the world to celebrate Diwali, the Festival of Lights — marking the triumph of light over darkness, good over evil,

6824daa35caf6638.title: Fifty years ago | Power struggle in China had begun 2 years ago
6824daa35caf6638.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 02:26 am IST Tokyo, November 9: Though the ouster from power of the four Shanghai radicals, led by Mao Tse-tung’s widow, Chiang Ching, became known to the outside world only last month, an acute power struggle within the Chinese Communist Party had been going on for nearly two years with Chairman Mao himself ranged against the gang of four, as they have now come to be known. Some light on this hitherto hidden aspect has been thrown by an editorial carried by the Liberation Army Daily, official organ of the People’s Liberation Army. According to the editorial, the gang of four had been engaging over a period of time in an attempt to usurp top party and State leadership. Mao, however, saw through the plot and made it impossible for their schemes to be achieved. 766d5dd61af4ec7c.title: Optional Travel Insurance Scheme urged for railway staff
766d5dd61af4ec7c.summary: Published - November 10, 2026 12:24 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Senior National Railway Trade Union leader and Divisional Railway Users’ Consultative Committee (DRUCC) member Chalasani Gandhi on Tuesday urged the Railway Board to extend the Optional Travel Insurance Scheme (OTIS) to serving railway employees, pensioners, and their eligible family members travelling on Privilege Passes and Privilege Ticket Orders (PTOs). Mr. Gandhi stated in a release that following directions from the Supreme Court the Railway Board had extended the optional travel insurance facility – previously restricted to online ticket bookings – to passengers purchasing reserved tickets through Railway Passenger Reservation System (PRS) counters with effect from October 27. Under the scheme, passengers receive an accident insurance coverage of up to ₹10 lakh against a nominal premium of 45 paise. The scheme covers compensation for death, permanent disability, hospitalisation expenses, and transportation of mortal remains. Questioning the rationale behind excluding railway personnel from the welfare measure, Mr. Gandhi stressed that railway employees face constant risks while rendering dedicated service. Extending the insurance protection to employees and their families booking tickets online or via PRS counters on Passes and PTOs would benefit lakhs of railway families nationwide. He urged the Railway Board to issue necessary policy amendments allowing staff and their dependents to opt for the insurance by paying the standard premium, while establishing clear guidelines for policy issuance and claim settlements. ca4cec0548bff88f.title: Trump, in CBS interview, says deportation policy was ‘too tough’
ca4cec0548bff88f.summary: Published - November 09, 2026 04:52 am IST - WASHINGTON U.S. President Donald Trump. | Photo Credit: AP U.S. President Donald Trump said that his mass deportation of undocumented immigrants was "too tough," according to an excerpt of an interview with CBS aired on Sunday (November 8, 2026). Asked about his deportation policy, Mr. Trump told CBS ' "60 Minutes": "I think it was too tough...I think it might be too tough." The excerpt was published by CBS on X ahead of a broadcast of the interview on network TV later on Sunday (November 8, 2026). It was recorded after the Republican Party's heavy loss in midterm elections on Tuesday. While Mr. Trump has won some domestic support for securing the U.S. southern border, his administration's aggressive push to deport millions of undocumented migrants has drawn widespread criticism. However, Mr. Trump on Friday (November 6, 2026) appointed the architect of that hardline policy, Stephen Miller, as his chief of staff, signalling a bare-knuckle fightback after the Republican election loss. Mr. Miller has been synonymous with scenes of masked immigration agents committing violence after he backed federal agents who shot and killed two Americans early this year. The Congress party's receipts from donations above ₹20,000 plunged nearly 75% to ₹130.69 crore in 2025-26 , the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows. Delhi was enveloped in a haze of toxic air on the morning of Deepavali , with the city's air quality nearing the 'severe' category with an Air Quality Index (AQI) reading of 383. This opening marks the subsidiary's first physical expansion beyond California, with its US branches now at eight locations. The inauguration ceremony was led by SBI Group Chairman Challa Sreenivasulu Setty, alongside Consul General of India in Houston, DC Manjunath and Frisco Mayor Mark Hill. Located in the rapidly growing North Dallas region, the new Frisco branch is designed to offer a full suite of retail and business banking services. ea705bc56d367b72.title: Bullion may remain under pressure as markets track US-Iran war, inflation
ea705bc56d367b72.summary: Bullion prices are likely to remain under pressure next week as investors track developments in the US-Iran conflict, movements in crude oil prices and inflation data for cues on the outlook for interest rates, analysts said. The focus will be on inflation prints from China, the US, Germany, Japan and India. Investors will also closely track speeches by Federal Reserve officials and US employment data. Chinese economic indicators will be important for industrial metals, they added. Geopolitical developments will remain a key driver after US President Donald Trump confirmed fresh military strikes on Iran, while claiming that Washington had made "a lot of progress" in negotiations with Tehran, adding another layer of uncertainty. The domestic commodities market will remain closed during the morning session on Tuesday due to Diwali-Balipratipada. 2c2cc6acf539af85.title: Assam OIL facility fire: death toll rises to four as another injured dies; four suspended
2c2cc6acf539af85.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 07:21 pm IST - Dibrugarh (Assam) Workers move away as a massive fire rages following an explosion at Oil India Limited's (OIL) Intermediate Tank Farm (ITF), in Dibrugarh district, on November 6, 2026. | Photo Credit: PTI The toll in the fire incident at an Oil India Ltd (OIL) facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district increased to four with another injured worker succumbing on Sunday (November 8, 2026), while the PSU has suspended all four of its personnel who were in charge of the site, officials said. Three people who were also injured in the blaze on Friday (November 6, 2026) are undergoing treatment in a critical condition. All the victims were employees of Spectron Engineering Private Limited, a Mumbai-based company engaged by OIL. One person was killed in the fire on the day of the incident, while two died the next day. A mechanical helper, Sailen Gogoi, who was undergoing treatment at a private hospital here, died during the day, taking the toll to four, the official said. A fire had broken out on November 6 after an explosion during maintenance work at OIL's intermediate tank farm (ITF) in Tengakhat, the public sector undertaking said in a statement. An ITF is a facility where petroleum products are temporarily stored in tanks before being transferred for further processing or transportation. Meanwhile, OIL has instituted a high-level inquiry to probe into the incident, another official said. The committee has put all four OIL employees who were in-charge of the ITF, including three officers, on suspension, he said. "They were placed under suspension until the investigation is over," the official added. The PSU has announced an ex-gratia of ₹10 lakh to the next of kin of each deceased, and Rs 5 lakh to each injured person. Union minister Sarbananda Sonowal and Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma were closely monitoring the situation, the PSU said on Saturday (November 7, 2026). 7aa18d1186eefc6c.title: Anuj Shrivatri becomes India’s 100th chess Grandmaster
7aa18d1186eefc6c.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 09:10 pm IST Anuj Shrivatri also became the first GM from Madhya Pradesh. Credit: X/@ChessbaseIndia Anuj Shrivatri on Sunday (November 8, 2026) became India’s 100th chess Grandmaster, by winning the 7th ASEAN+ Individual Open chess championship in Ozamiz City, the Philippines. The 22-year-old Anuj also became the first GM from Madhya Pradesh. He won the tournament with seven points from nine rounds after suffering a loss in the opening round. His triumph enabled him earn the GM title. The legendary Viswanathan Anand had become the country’s first Grandmaster in 1988. The wait for the 100th GM was watched intently after S. Aswath and V.S. Rathanvel recently became the 98th and 99th GMs respectively. 4f440a6990bb54de.title: NGT issues notice to Tirunelveli Collector over threats to Tamirabharani fish species
4f440a6990bb54de.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 07:06 pm IST - CHENNAI Some of the fishes found in the Tamirabharani River in Tirunelveli district. File | Photo Credit: Special arrangement The Principal Bench of the National Green Tribunal (NGT), New Delhi, has issued notice to the Tirunelveli Collector and five others over threats faced by fish species in Tamirabharani River due to pollution and habitat loss. Taking suo motu cognisance of a report, titled ‘Tamirabharani’s Endemic Fish Face Threats From Pollution, Habitat Loss’, published in The Hindu on September 28, the Bench, comprising Justice Arun Kumar Tyagi and expert members A. Senthil Vel and Afroz Ahamed, directed that the Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board, the Central Pollution Control Board’s Regional Office in Chennai, Ashoka Trust for Research in Ecology and the Environment (ATREE), and Agasthyamalai Community Conservation Centre (ACCC) be impleaded as respondents, besides the Collector. The order said: “The above news item attracts the provisions of the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, the Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974, and the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, and prima facie raises substantial questions relating to the environment arising out of the implementation of the enactments specified in Schedule I to the National Green Tribunal Act, 2010.” The Bench directed the Registry to list the matter before the Southern Bench of the Tribunal, Chennai, on January 22, 2027, as the cause of action had arisen within its territorial jurisdiction. It also directed the respondents to file their responses before the Bench at least one day ahead of the date of hearing. The Hindu had reported that 125 fish species had been identified in upstream, midstream and lower estuarine stretches of the river. Seven of them are endemic to the Tamirabharani. Japan's Meteorological Agency put the quake's magnitude at 5.7, while the US Geological Survey reported it at magnitude 5.5. Smaller aftershocks were reported. f1fb36e5c6e7e558.title: Congress donations fall nearly 75%, sharpest decline in a decade
f1fb36e5c6e7e558.summary: The Congress party's receipts from donations above Rs 20,000 plunged nearly 75 per cent to Rs 130.69 crore in 2025-26, the steepest annual fall in such contributions in a decade, an analysis of the party's filings with the Election Commission shows. The party had received Rs 517.39 crore in such contributions in 2024-25, according to its 2024-25 contribution report submitted to the commission. A comparison with the preceding 12 financial years shows that the last steeper fall was in 2015-16, when Congress' disclosed donations dropped roughly 86 per cent from Rs 141.46 crore the previous year. The latest decline follows two years of higher collections. Congress received Rs 281.48 crore in disclosed donations in 2023-24, rising to Rs 517.39 crore in 2024-25, the year Lok Sabha elections were held. BJP received Rs 6,074.02 crore in donations exceeding Rs 20,000 in 2024-25, nearly 12 times Congress's collection. BJP's corresponding figure for 2025-26 is not available as the party's ...

The air quality is forecast to turn 'severe' on Monday following Diwali celebrations, combined with vehicular emissions, as well as the peak stubble-burning season. Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data on Sunday, air quality was in the 'severe' category at 12 and in the 'very poor' category at 22. The worst AQI was recorded in Jahangirpuri at 463. The city's average AQI increased from 369 on Saturday to 376 on Sunday, remaining not far from the 'severe' threshold of 400. 4eaa140d0d65a62f.title: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
4eaa140d0d65a62f.summary: Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago, according to confidential data held by the country’s statistics agency, Rosstat.
4eaa140d0d65a62f.headline_en: Hacked Records Show 400,000 Russians Killed in War on Ukraine
4eaa140d0d65a62f.raw_facts: Russia has recorded the deaths of about 400,000 of its people fighting in Ukraine since the full-scale invasion almost five years ago, according to confidential data held by the country’s statistics agency, Rosstat.
flags: Timeline inconsistency: The full-scale invasion began in February 2022. As of mid-2024, it has been approximately two years, not 'almost five years'.

Source reliability: The claim attributes the data to 'confidential data held by Rosstat' revealed via 'hacked records'. While independent estimates (e.g., from BBC, Mediazona, or Western intelligence) have suggested Russian casualties in the hundreds of thousands, there is no verified public evidence that Rosstat's internal records were hacked and released with this specific figure.

Official vs. Independent Data: Rosstat has not officially released a figure of 400,000 deaths. Official Russian figures have historically been much lower or non-specific. Independent estimates vary widely but often fall in the range of 100,000 to 200,000+ confirmed deaths, with total casualties (including wounded) being higher. A confirmed death toll of 400,000 is on the higher end of speculative estimates and lacks a verified primary source in this context.

Unverified 'Hacked Records': Claims of hacked government statistics are common in disinformation or unverified leaks. Without a credible, independent verification of the hack and the data's authenticity, this claim is highly suspect.

d8b9db3849d886ba.title: Tamil Nadu CM orders rollout of free laptop scheme for college students
d8b9db3849d886ba.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has ordered the implementation of the 'Vetri Laptop Scheme' for college students, and Rs 2,000 crore is the allocation for the initiative, the state government said on Saturday. A high-level committee will be formed under the chief minister's leadership for implementing the free laptop scheme, announced in the 2026-27 budget, for college students. First and second-year UG, diploma students studying in government and state-aided colleges in a string of courses, including medicine, agriculture, and law, will benefit from the free laptop scheme, the government said in an official release.

2a345b559a500f58.title: Amber Enterprises arm IL JIN Electronics files DRHP for ₹2,500 crore IPO
2a345b559a500f58.summary: IL JIN Electronics (India) Ltd, an arm of Amber Enterprises India Ltd, has filed preliminary papers with the market regulator Sebi to raise Rs 2,500 crore through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO is entirely a fresh issue of equity shares, with no offer for sale (OFS) component, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. The company plans to use the proceeds to repay or prepay certain outstanding borrowings, including accrued interest, availed by the company and its subsidiaries, Ascent Circuits and Shogini Technoarts. The funds will also be used to purchase plant, machinery, and equipment for its manufacturing units, as well as for general corporate purposes. e1aca824ee4dabc0.title: Sustainable Development Council unveils nationwide citizen driven initiative for sustainable India
e1aca824ee4dabc0.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 12:48 am IST - CHENNAI Ministers P. Venkataramanan and B. Rajkumar unveiling the Sustainable Development Council’s MyBharat2030, a nationwide citizen-driven survey initiative in Chennai. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement The Sustainable Development Council (SDC), an international non-profit organisation holding Special Consultative Status with the United Nations Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC), unveiled MyBharat2030, a nationwide citizen-driven survey initiative at the 2nd World Cities Day Connect 2026 in Chennai recently. According to a press release, MyBharat2030 seeks to understand people’s aspirations, capture their perspectives and assess collective progress towards the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The initiative marks a significant step towards strengthening citizen engagement in India’s journey towards a progressive, inclusive and sustainable future. The initiative was inaugurated in the presence of P. Venkataramanan, Minister for Food and Civil Supplies; B. Rajkumar, Minister for Housing and Urban Development, and Sowmiya Anbumani, MLA and president of the PMK’s Pasumai Thayagam. Amudhavalli Ranganathan, Chairperson (India), Sustainable Development Council; Datchanamoorthy Ramu, founder-president; and Gokulnath Mathiyazhagan, secretary-general were among those present on the occasion. Published - November 08, 2026 12:47 am IST

98fad76f3fea8d54.title: Odisha CM Mohan Majhi cancels Diwali celebrations over Cyclone Arnab damage
98fad76f3fea8d54.summary: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi has cancelled Diwali celebrations at his residence this year in view of the damage and suffering caused by Cyclone Arnab and subsequent floods in several parts of the state. In a statement, the Chief Minister's Office (CMO) said Diwali celebrations at Majhi's residence have been cancelled. The CM has also requested people not to bring gifts or bouquets on the occasion. "The Hon'ble Chief Minister has appealed to people to remain sensitive to the public in the affected areas and extend a helping hand to those affected by the disaster," the CMO said in a post on X. 73f51ce4601d74a1.title: South Africa mourns Indian-origin TV pioneer Ramprakash Gopidayal
73f51ce4601d74a1.summary: Tributes poured in for South African Indian-origin media personality Ramprakash Gopidayal, who pioneered television programmes and radio recordings for the local Indian community, as he was cremated on Friday after succumbing to illness a day before. Popularly known as Ramu, Gopidayal, despite being an introverted, camera-shy man, started the first television programme for the Indian community, 'Impressions', on national state broadcaster South African Broadcasting Corporation (SABC), in the apartheid era. He first joined the SABC as its first Indian-origin technician in 1980. With apartheid waning, the SABC started 'Impressions', a weekly magazine programme on TV for the Indian community, in 1986. It fell upon Gopidayal to take on the task of starting an unprecedented programme from scratch. Satheesan said here on Saturday (November 7) that the country’s best disaster management and resilience programme would be implemented in Keralam. The two female students have been barred from taking admission in any course at the university in the future. The university had formed a committee to investigate the matter and has checked CCTV footage of the campus and heard from various stakeholders to come to a decision. One of them is a current student and the other was an ex-student who had finished her post-graduate course a few months back. “Two students have been expelled from the studentship/post-studentship academic activities. 7a6420786d89b00e.title: Chennai Mayor condemns workers using bare hands to clear Deepavali waste, silt
7a6420786d89b00e.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:39 am IST - Chennai Workers clear a silt catch pit with bare hands and without protective gloves or boots in Jamalia, Perambur, amid the Northeast monsoon rains, highlighting the lack of adequate safety gear for Greater Chennai Corporation workers on November 2, 2026. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement With crackers and other Deepavali waste being cleared from streets across Chennai, conservancy workers of the Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) continue to handle silt, garbage and stagnant water without adequate protective equipment, raising concerns over their safety during the Northeast monsoon. A recent report in The Hindu highlighted how workers who were engaged to clear silt from stormwater drain (SWD) catch pits and stagnant water in several parts of the city were working with bare hands, without any protective gear -- gloves and footwear. The practice was also noticed during the recent rains, where workers were seen clearing silt from a catch pit without gloves. Mayor R. Priya said the practice should not continue and pointed out that the waste generated during Deepavali, including discarded crackers, posed additional challenges for workers. “This should not be happening,” she said, adding that cracker waste could contain chemicals and required separate cleaning arrangements rather than being mixed with regular garbage. A GCC official acknowledged that the provisions made for safety equipment in the estimates were inadequate. “Invariably, sewage gets mixed with stormwater drains, whatever we may say. The provisions made in the estimates are very limited and are largely based on the number of man-days. From next time onwards, we will make more liberal provisions for safety gear and incur some additional expenditure, as it is necessary for the workers’ safety,” the official said. Mao Ning, a spokesperson for the Chinese foreign ministry, said at a press briefing this week in Beijing that China "is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state." Nothing is set, but the three-leader gathering would take place this month on the sidelines of a regional summit in Shenzhen. If it happens, it would be historic. Following his retirement, "the Board has appointed him as Chairman Emeritus of the Company with effect from November 12, 2026," said Voltas, a Tata Group firm, in its regulatory filing. eabbfaffceff3701.title: Students urged to dream big, prepare for a self-reliant India
eabbfaffceff3701.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:17 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Students should dare to dream big, think independently and pursue ambitious goals to drive innovation and contribute to the vision of a self-reliant India, said Prof. Ramesh Srikonda, Director of the School of Planning and Architecture, Vijayawada. Addressing the Freshers’ Day celebrations at Dr. RVR NRI Institute of Technology (Deemed to be University), he emphasised that bold aspirations lead to new ideas and innovative outcomes. He urged students to focus on holistic development rather than limiting their ambitions to obtaining academic degrees. The celebrations, organised to welcome newly admitted first-year students, witnessed the participation of over 2,000 students, who showcased their talents through colourful singing and dancing performances. Prof. M.L.N. Rao, Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor of Rajiv Gandhi University of Knowledge Technologies (RGUKT-AP), said emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning and Quantum Technologies would drive major transformations over the next five to 10 years. He encouraged students to prepare themselves to contribute to the visions of Swarna Andhra Pradesh 2047 and Viksit Bharat 2047. NRI University Chairman and Chancellor Dr. Ravi Venkata Rao said the institution’s four-year academic programme aimed at shaping students into responsible, capable individuals equipped to overcome challenges and contribute meaningfully to society. Vice-Chancellor Dr. K.R.S. Sambasiva Rao urged students to make effective use of the university’s teaching and learning facilities and continuously upgrade their skills to become industry-ready professionals. Organising convener and Dean D. Suneetha, CEO, Pro-Vice-Chancellors, Registrar, Deans, Heads of Departments, faculty members and other dignitaries attended the celebrations. f086a0b616aada4a.title: D2C brands see 27% more orders ahead of Diwali; sales value up 45%: Report
f086a0b616aada4a.summary: Direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands in India shipped 27 per cent more orders a day in the run-up to Diwali this year than in the same period last year, while the value of goods sold jumped about 45 per cent, according to a report. ClickPost, an AI logistics automation and post-purchase platform for D2C and retail, analysed more than 8 crore orders placed on the websites of nearly 400 D2C brands. It compared the festive shopping windows of September 20 to November 5 this year and September 1 to October 17 last year. According to ClickPost's report, gross merchandise value (GMV), the total value of goods sold, grew about 1.7 times faster than the number of orders. The report said this was because shoppers bought higher-priced products despite rising retail prices, rather than looking for cheaper alternatives. Spending was concentrated in high-value categories such as luxury fashion, skincare, wellness and jewellery, it said. Despite the higher volumes, deliveries became more reliable. .

b6955c13846247d1.title: Centre counters Karnataka's E20 claims, says samples meet quality standards
b6955c13846247d1.summary: The government on Saturday defended the 20 per cent ethanol-blended petrol programme, saying tests of 893 samples collected across 27 states and Union Territories, including 56 in Karnataka, found them compliant with prescribed quality standards, as state-run oil companies challenged the Karnataka government's claims of excessive ethanol content in fuel sold at some retail outlets. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, in a statement, said Indian Oil Corporation (IOC), Bharat Petroleum Corporation (BPCL) and Hindustan Petroleum Corporation (HPCL) had found ethanol content in all 893 samples within the prescribed 19-21 per cent range under the Bureau of Indian Standards' IS 17021 specification. The 56 samples tested in Karnataka, covering different locations and all three oil marketing companies (OMCs), recorded ethanol content of 19-20 per cent, averaging 19.30 per cent, the ministry said. The findings directly contradict a recent press release by Karnataka's Department of Food

e85d14ba92076f05.title: Nallur toll plaza on Kolkata National Highway to be moved to Durainallur
e85d14ba92076f05.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 01:39 am IST - CHENNAI The National Highways Authority of India has planned to shift the toll plaza at Nallur on the Chennai - Kolkata National Highway. It will be moved to Durainallur, which is about 13 km from the present location. The plaza is notorious for long waits during rush hours. Motorists fed up with waiting at the Nallur Plaza will get some relief from this move. “Residents of areas such as Karanodai, Janapanchathiram, Nallur and Periyapalayam will find it very convenient when the plaza is removed. There are several colleges in the area and the buses transporting students too wait in queue to cross the plaza on many occasions. Shifting of the plaza has been a long-time demand,” said K. Suresh Kumar, a resident. Ramesh, another resident, suggested that the width of the road be narrowed at that location. “It is now wider than the road width, making it difficult to cross. It would be helpful if the road stretch is normalised and shops regularised,” he said. Sources in the NHAI said that the existing location was no longer viable as a number of new roads have been laid in the surroundings making it possible for road users to avoid the plaza. This will lead to loss of revenue. “The plaza is also located inside municipal limits, making it pertinent to shift it outside. The contract of the current agency managing the plaza will get over by May next year. We hope to get the design ready for the new plaza by then,” explained a source. Around 50,000 passenger car units use that road on a daily basis. The plaza is also likely to be a multi-lane free flow tolling system without toll booths and operators. It will be moved to Durainallur, which is about 13 km from the present location. The plaza is notorious for long waits during rush hours. Motorists fed up with waiting at the Nallur Plaza will get some relief from this move. “Residents of areas such as Karanodai, Janapanchathiram, Nallur and Periyapalayam will find it very convenient when the plaza is removed. There are several colleges in the area and the buses transporting students too wait in queue to cross the plaza on many occasions. Shifting of the plaza has been a long-time demand,” said K. Suresh Kumar, a resident. Ramesh, another resident, suggested that the width of the road be narrowed at that location. “It is now wider than the road width, making it difficult to cross. It would be helpful if the road stretch is normalised and shops regularised,” he said. Sources in the NHAI said that the existing location was no longer viable as a number of new roads have been laid in the surroundings making it possible for road users to avoid the plaza. This will lead to loss of revenue. “The plaza is also located inside municipal limits, making it pertinent to shift it outside. The contract of the current agency managing the plaza will get over by May next year. We hope to get the design ready for the new plaza by then,” explained a source. Around 50,000 passenger car units use that road on a daily basis. The plaza is also likely to be a multi-lane free flow tolling system without toll booths and operators. bf7eb2a5cf5df45f.title: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings files draft papers with Sebi for IPO
bf7eb2a5cf5df45f.summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd (HCCH), backed by The Coca-Cola Company and Jubilant Beverages, has filed its draft papers with the market regulator Sebi to raise funds through an initial public offering (IPO). The proposed IPO will be entirely an offer for sale (OFS) of up to 99,74,61,456 equity shares by promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte Ltd, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) dated November 6. Since the issue is entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO, with the entire proceeds going to the selling shareholder.

fc952079d179daed.title: Shami defined an era of pace bowling: BCCI
fc952079d179daed.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:56 am IST - NEW DELHI Mohammed Shami in action. File | Photo Credit: Nirmal Harindran The BCCI on Saturday paid a glowing tribute Mohammad Shami, saying the wily India pacer defined an era of pace bowling in Test cricket. Shami announced his retirement from Test cricket on Friday night. He ended his Test journey with 229 wickets from 64 matches, making him the sixth most successful pacer in Tests for the country behind Kapil Dev (434), Zaheer Khan, Ishant Sharma (both 311), Javagal Srinath (236), Jasprit Bumrah (234). "Thank you for defining an era of Indian pace bowling, Test Cap #279," wrote the BCCI on social media. Former India cricketers also joined in to congratulate Shami on a successful red ball career. Ravi Shastri believes Shami had more red ball cricket left in him. "Incredible career. I was lucky that I was the coach at that time. He was instrumental in India doing well. Without him the fast bowling unit would not have functioned. No one presented the seam better than him in world cricket. You could say James Anderson as well. If Shami did not get the wickets, he would still keep the pressure on the opposition. "Sad to see him go. I definitely though he had another 30-40 wickets left in him. He should have played in the last 12 months. May be should have been on this New Zealand tour as a Test match bowler," Shastri told the host broadcaster during the second ODI in New Zealand. "Many congratulations on your wonderful red ball cricket career @MdShami11. Your late movement with that cherry will be missed," wrote Pathan. "You will be Missed in Whites Buddy, congratulations on your amazing career. See you soon in Blues," added another former India pacer Munaf Patel. His Bengal teammate Manoj Tiwary said it was an honour playing alongside Shami. b5fa67bed2340462.summary: Polling places closed on Saturday after the final day of voting in New Zealand's election following a tense campaign that left the main contenders neck and neck with no clear route to victory for either. An incumbent conservative government led by the National party is seeking a second term against a leftwing bloc led by Labour. In polls close to election day, neither Prime Minister Christopher Luxon of National nor opposition leader Chris Hipkins of Labour had a clear path to victory, with minor parties on the ideological flanks expected to hold sway over the next government's formation. Voting began on October 26 and ended on Saturday at 7 pm. New Zealand's Electoral Commission aimed to release a count of 5 per cent of the vote within 30 minutes of polls closing.
