e413be16791dc88d.title: 42 days of SRFTI protest; classes suspended till December 11
e413be16791dc88d.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:56 am IST - KOLKATA The agitation at the Satyajit Ray Film & Television Institute (SRFTI) continued for 42 days as class suspension was extended till December 11, affecting academic life. Students of the film institute on Saturday (November 7, 2026) said that “This Diwali we choose to resist”, while authorities said they were “keen" to resume classes. “Diwali has always been a special occasion at SRFTI... But this year, the familiar celebrations are overshadowed by fear, uncertainty and an ongoing struggle for justice,” an official post by the SRFTI student union said on Saturday (November 7, 2026), a day before Deepavali. They also said that the day they are served justice will be Deepavali for them. “While the faculty and administration are ready to resume classes, a section of students continues to remain disengaged from academics and disrupt the functioning of the Institute through repeated violations of its rules and orders,” Registrar Deepak Kumar told The Hindu on Saturday (November 7, 2026). He further added that they are asking students to come forward for constructive dialogue. As of November 7, at least 25 students have received show cause notices, with 11 of them receiving them last Thursday (November 5, 2026). Six students have faced rustication, and one FIR has been registered against student union Vice-President Shubham. Shubham is one of the six students who got the rustication notice for allegedly vandalising the Vice-Chancellor Santosh Ajmeera’s office and manhandling him. However, all of these allegations have been denied by the students. According to the students, two contractual faculty members, and five resource persons of SRFTI have also been terminated from their jobs for showing solidarity with the students. As the classes remained suspended, the hostels and mess were also closed for students. 73d8046d11b387ed.title: Mathematics key to AI’s advancement, says expert
73d8046d11b387ed.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:35 pm IST - VIJAYAWADA Mathematics forms the backbone of modern artificial intelligence (AI), with advanced AI capabilities, predictive power and logical reasoning deeply rooted in mathematical equations, frameworks and data algorithms, said Reheena Nasrin of Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET) in Dhaka, Bangladesh. Addressing the valedictory session of a three-day international conference on “Computation Science and Intelligent Engineering”, organised by the Department of Mathematics in Siddhartha Academy of Higher Education (Deemed-to-be-University), she emphasised that strong mathematical foundations would remain essential for the future advancement of digital intelligence. The final-day technical sessions featured lectures by eminent experts. G. Sobhalatha of Sri Krishnadevaraya University, Anantapur, spoke on ‘Lexicographic Product Graph’, while Bukke Kiran Naik, a scientist from the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Rourkela, delivered a lecture on ‘Intelligent Thermodynamics’, focusing on data-driven systems optimisation and energy-water nexus solutions. Conference convener Charan announced that more than 200 research papers had been presented by academicians and researchers from reputed universities across India, reflecting the conference’s contribution to academic research and knowledge exchange. Certificates of participation and excellence were distributed to the paper presenters by the dignitaries. The valedictory session was attended by Vice-Chancellor P. Venkateswara Rao, Pro-Vice-Chancellor A.V. Ratna Prasad, dean D. Venkata Rao and registrar M. Ravichand. Head of the Mathematics Department Ch. Baby Rani, senior faculty members K. Hemalatha, J. Siva Ram Prasad and M.V.D.N.S. Madhavi, other faculty members, department heads, research scholars and students also participated in the programme. 39661e7999ffb000.title: Three investors offload 1.84% stake in Groww for ₹2,457 crore in bulk deals
39661e7999ffb000.summary: Peak XV Partners, Y Combinator and Goldman Sachs have sold a combined 2 per cent stake in Billionbrains Garage Ventures, the parent company of Groww, for Rs 2,457 crore, according to bulk deal data on the BSE and NSE. The three investors offloaded more than 11.52 crore shares, representing a combined 1.84 per cent stake in Groww on Friday, as per the data. US-based Peak XV Partners, through its arm Peak XV Partners Investments VI-1, sold more than 6 crore shares, and Goldman Sachs divested 4,380 shares of Groww on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). In addition, Y Combinator, through its arm YC Holdings II, LLC, disposed of 5.50 crore shares on the BSE. The shares were disposed of in the price range of Rs 211.09-215.20 apiece, taking the combined deal value to Rs 2,456.87 crore. Meanwhile, Goldman Sachs purchased 3.55 crore shares worth over Rs 764 crore. Details of other buyers of Groww's shares could not be identified on the exchanges. d607e15879d0bb8d.title: Bengaluru Metro conducts trial run of Blue Line train at Byappanahalli depot
d607e15879d0bb8d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 11:42 pm IST - Bengaluru Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) conducted a trial run of a train on the test track at the Byappanahalli depot on Saturday as part of preparations for the much-awaited Blue Line. The trial involved checking electrical systems, assessing the readiness of rolling stock and identifying possible infringements along the track. BMRCL is expected to move testing to the main line shortly. An official said that the testing would resume next week, subject to the availability of workers following Deepavali. Bharat Earth Movers Limited (BEML) has manufactured the driverless trainset for the Blue Line. The Blue Line, comprising Metro Phases 2A and 2B, is a major infrastructure project connecting the city with Kempegowda International Airport. The K.R. Puram–airport stretch is 38.44-km long, while the K.R. Puram–Central Silk Board section covers 19.75 km. 7a6a76cada888f6f.title: DMK flays govt.’s decision to remit money in lieu of distributing rice to ration cardholders in U.T.
7a6a76cada888f6f.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 03:04 am IST - PUDUCHERRY Convenor of DMK’s Puducherry unit R. Siva has flayed the AINRC-BJP government for adopting the cash transfer mode instead of distributing free rice under the scheme in the Union Territory. In a statement, the DMK leader said the government had not distributed free rice through ration shops for the last nine months. Now, the government has remitted money into the accounts of ration cardholders in lieu of free rice meant for six months. The amount remitted by the government was based on a calculation of ₹43 per kg for the rice, he said. However, the cash remitted was not sufficient for buying rice due to cost escalation. The price of rice has gone up substantially in the open market and the money given by the government would be inadequate for the residents to buy the required quantity, he said. “The government’s decision to adopt Direct Benefit Transfer mode was a betrayal of the mandate given by the people. The Chief Minister had promised the voters to provide rice through ration shops. If the implementation of the scheme to distribute rice through ration shops would take more time, the government should remit more money considering the market rate of rice,” Mr. Siva said. 78b4dd6ccab6540f.title: Renovated bus terminus in Ranipet town opened for public use
78b4dd6ccab6540f.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:57 am IST - RANIPET Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspect the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. | Photo Credit: Special Arrangement After more than four years of renovation work, the restored ₹13.55-crore integrated bus terminus on the Ranipet-Walajah Main Road was opened for public use, ahead of Deepavali. Officials of Ranipet municipality, which executed the multi-crore work, said that the old terminus was built more than five decades ago with very few facilities for commuters. “The restored terminus helps people board long-distance buses. The facility has better seating arrangements and safety features for commuters,” said S. Kumar, a commuter. Funded under Kalaignar Nagarpura Membattu Thittam 2022-23 that aims to fulfil the infrastructural gaps in the urban local bodies, work to restore the terminus was started in 2022. “The restored bus terminus will help commuters, especially women and senior citizens to board buses safely as round-the-clock surveillance is in place. A help desk is also available to guide commuters,” said D. Senthil Kumar, Commissioner, Ranipet municipality. Collector N. Priya Ravichandran inspected the restored bus terminus in the town in the presence of transport and municipal officials. The restored bus terminus will operate buses to Bengaluru, Vellore, Vandavasi, Cheyyar, Chengam, Arcot, Ranipet, Coimbatore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Hosur, and Dharmapuri. Among civic amenities, the terminus has a purified drinking water facility, solar-powered LED streetlights, digital timing boards, feeding room, a police booth, and CCTV cameras. A police outpost will also be set up in the coming days. Every day, on an average, more than 200 buses operated by Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation ply from the terminus. Commuters said that additional buses to towns such as Tiruvannamalai, Sholinghur, Arcot, Gingee, and Kancheepuram should be operated at the terminus. Publ

2052a510689062eb.title: Greek-themed Salaam Souk to be held at Palace Grounds in Bengaluru on November 8
2052a510689062eb.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:56 am IST - Bengaluru The Karnataka Tourism Department is supporting, ‘Salaam Souk – The Big Fat Greek Souk’, an event showcasing the colours, cuisine, music and Mediterranean culture of Greece to people in Bengaluru. Scheduled to be held on November 8 in Palace Grounds, the event marks the eighth edition of Salaam Souk and its first Greek-themed edition. It is an initiative of The Tribe & Co that has previously presented cultural themes inspired by Morocco, Turkey, Uzbekistan, India and Dubai. The festival has been designed to recreate the feel of a Greek street market, combining Mediterranean-inspired food, fashion, art, music, home décor, beauty and wellness experiences. The event will feature 35 food stalls, 150 retail stalls, live bands, fire shows and aerial performances, offering visitors a distinctive Greek-inspired cultural experience in Bengaluru. 8464144f1a0e52ff.title: 108 ambulance network geared up to handle emergencies
8464144f1a0e52ff.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:55 am IST - CHENNAI In view of Deepavali, the 108 ambulance network is prepared to handle all types of emergencies. All ambulances across the State have been strategically positioned at identified hotspots to ensure that emergency care reaches the needy at the earliest. According to a press release, this proactive deployment will help in minimising the response time and thereby increasing the life-saved percentage. The network, especially in metro cities, has clocked an average response time of less than seven minutes, and is focused on sustaining and further improving the same. The “EMRI GHS 108 Ambulance Services”, based on the previous year experiences, have taken precautionary measures with regard to deployment of ambulances in identified Deepavali hotspot areas, where more number of fire/ burns and assault cases are expected in the respective locations. Last year, the network received 26,000 calls requiring emergency services across Tamil Nadu during Deepavali. The Emergency Response Centre for helplines 108, 104 and 102 are working with full strength under three shifts. All support staff are working in coordination with respective district authorities, the release said. A medical protocol is being developed to transfer the patient based on their criticality from a lower facility to a higher facility, while inter-hospital transfer of critical patients is earmarked through Advanced Life Support ambulances based on separate despatch criteria. A dedicated Inter Facility Transfer help desk is also functioning, the release said. 73b93f68cba29107.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:03 am IST - Bengaluru The university has created a separate WhatsApp group that includes the principals and placement officers from all colleges under its purview. | Photo Credit: Getty Images To provide employment opportunities to its students, Bangalore University plans to establish placement cells in all the undergraduate and postgraduate colleges under its jurisdiction. Through these cells, the university will conduct placement drives, besides holding offline and online skill training essential for employment. While the university already has a placement cell that conducts annual placement drives, and has even appointed placement officers in select affiliated colleges, these officers are currently not active. Allegations have surfaced that, as a result, students are not receiving adequate information regarding placements. “When enrolling in colleges, students and parents place high priority on placements. However, in the current scenario, job availability is limited. Also, students lack accurate information about the jobs that are available. While we conduct placement activities within the university, it is difficult to ensure that students across all our affiliated colleges benefit from them. Therefore, our university will establish placement cells in all 274 government and private colleges under its jurisdiction,” said Sarvamangala, Director, Pre-Examination Coaching Centre & Placement Cell, Bangalore University. The university has created a separate WhatsApp group that includes the principals and placement officers from all colleges under its purview. “Every day, we receive various updates regarding placements from government, corporate, and private organisations. 59f706d6e2da936e.title: Rahul questions E20 petrol ethanol levels, cites Karnataka test results
59f706d6e2da936e.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Saturday attacked the Modi government over the rollout of E20 petrol, citing test results of samples collected by the Karnataka government, and asked the Centre to come clean on the actual ethanol content in fuel being sold across the country. In a post in Hindi on X, Gandhi said, "E20 turned into 420 stealing petrol from the public's cars!" The reference was to Section 420 of the erstwhile Indian Penal Code, which dealt with cheating. Gandhi said the government claims that petrol contains 20 per cent ethanol but tests conducted on samples collected from seven districts in Karnataka had revealed higher levels. "The Karnataka government collected petrol samples from 7 districts and had them tested at an accredited lab. Look at the results 11 out of 14 samples contained more than 20 per cent ethanol; 31.2 per cent at IOCL, 30.5 per cent at HPCL; IOCL, HPCL, BPCL, Nayara, Shell whether government-owned or private all exceeded the limit," he claimed.

74f5ce093329eb6c.title: Two youths arrested for possessing narcotics in Vellore
74f5ce093329eb6c.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST - VELLORE Two youths were arrested by Vellore South police for possession of 1300 narcotic tablets (Tapentadol) near the fort complex in Vellore town on Saturday. The police identified them as R. Vinoth, 23, and his friend B. Manimaran, 23. They were residents of Vellore town. Initial inquiry revealed that based on a tip-off to Vellore SP N.U. Sivaraman, special teams were formed to conduct surprise checks in public places in the district. During a surprise check near the fort complex, the team apprehended the suspects. They checked the duo and their bags, where they found a huge quantity of pharmaceutical drugs in them. Investigation found that the gang had placed an order for tablets with pharmacies online. The tablets were sent by couriers to them. The police said the duo were on their way to the railway station to go to Chennai, where they planned to sell the drugs. A case was registered and arrested persons were lodged in Central Prison in Vellore. A probe is under way. 37bb49dfea8ff924.title: Gang held near Vaniyambadi for burglary
37bb49dfea8ff924.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST - TIRUPATTUR A gang of five persons were arrested by Vaniyambadi Taluk police in Tirupattur on Saturday for stealing 52 sovereigns of gold jewellery, one kilogram of silver objects and around ₹20,000 lakh cash from the house of a painter recently. The arrested persons were identified as K. Naveen, 26, T. Parthiban, 30, S. Gopinath, 39, G. Manikandan, 40, and C. Sarathkumar, 25. They are previous offenders and have theft cases against them in Salem, Dharmapuri, Tirupattur, Thanjavur, and Pudukottai. Initial inquiry revealed that the victim, R. Prabhakaran, 39, was living with his family including wife Geetha (34) and mother Ambika (65) in the house near Vaniyambadi town a few days ago when the gang barged into the house. The police said the gang allegedly tied R. Prabhakaran, 39, and his family and stole the valuables from the house before fleeing the spot. Mr. Prabhakaran managed to untie himself and alerted Vaniyambadi Taluk police. Special teams were formed to nab the suspects. The police also analysed CCTV camera footage to identify suspects. The suspects were traced to a hideout in Thanjavur and were arrested. A car used by the gang was also seized. The police said that members of the gang befriended each other when they were serving jail sentences. They travel to various parts of the State and stay in a locality before indulging in burglary. A case was registered and a probe is under way. Published - November 08, 2026 12:54 am IST Terms & conditions | Institutional Subscriber Comments have to be in English, and in full sentences. ef79ad7ceb40913e.title: Techie arrested for attempting to snatch woman’s chain using pepper spray
ef79ad7ceb40913e.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:46 am IST - CHENNAI A 46-year-old project manager at an IT company was arrested for allegedly attacking a woman with pepper spray in an attempt to snatch her gold chain on a pedestrian footbridge near Tambaram Sanatorium. Police said he turned to chain snatching to repay debts accumulated through losses in online trading. The victim, Bhuvaneswari, 24, an MBA graduate from Chitlapakkam, works with a private financial firm in Tambaram. She was returning home after work when she stopped on the footbridge to distribute laddus to elderly destitute people. Police said the accused, Kuppusamy of Pammal, approached her and sprayed her face with pepper spray before attempting to snatch her gold chain. She raised an alarm, drawing the attention of passers-by, who caught and thrashed the suspect before handing him over to the Tambaram police. During interrogation, police found that Kuppusamy, a B. Com graduate, was employed as a project manager at a private IT firm on Old Mahabalipuram Road (OMR). Investigators found that he had suffered substantial losses in online trading and had sold his house in Pammal, valued at around ₹60 lakh, to clear his debts. However, he continued to face financial liabilities and allegedly attempted the robbery to raise more money. 5e25456018415d56.title: Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore removes books published by Agal Vilakku Pathipagam
5e25456018415d56.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:32 am IST - Coimbatore The Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore on Saturday took down books published by Agal Vilakku Pathipagam, which came under scrutiny following allegations of irregularities in procurement and questions about their content and authorship. Sources said the books were removed as visitors had been approaching the library to read them after the controversy came to light. On Friday, writer Perumal Murugan flagged inaccuracies and questionable authorship of certain titles at Periyar Arivulagam. He claimed the publisher had supplied around 1,800 titles to the library, priced much higher than other Tamil books. The issue has triggered a political row in the State since, with the DMK and ruling TVK charging each other with wrongdoing and corruption. Revenue from operations rose 35.39 per cent to Rs 3,676 crore during the second quarter of FY27 from Rs 2,715 crore a year earlier, it said. The company's net profit for the first half of the current fiscal year, however, declined 35.39 per cent to Rs 2,029 crore from Rs 2,568 crore in the year-ago period, the filing added.

34907735bc26c903.title: RPF steps up Deepavali vigil, apprehends five with firecrackers at Chennai Central, Egmore
34907735bc26c903.summary: Updated - November 08, 2026 01:50 am IST - CHENNAI With a view to ensuring passenger safety during the Deepavali festival, the Railway Protection Force (RPF), Chennai Division, Southern Railway, has intensified surveillance and preventive checks at major railway stations to curb illegal transportation of firecrackers and other inflammable materials. During special checks conducted on Friday, RPF personnel apprehended five persons carrying firecrackers at Chennai Central and Chennai Egmore railway stations in two separate operations. At Chennai Central, four persons were intercepted while attempting to board passenger trains with firecrackers. Three were stopped before boarding the Chennai Central–Jolarpettai Yelagiri Express, while another was intercepted before boarding the Chennai Central–Thiruvananthapuram Express. Four separate cases were registered against them under Section 164 of the Railways Act, 1989. At Chennai Egmore, RPF personnel apprehended a 25-year-old man carrying a box of firecrackers and registered a case under the same provision. Meanwhile, as part of its efforts to sensitise passengers ahead of Deepavali, the RPF conducted a Jan Jagaran awareness programme at Chennai Beach Railway Station on Friday. Passengers were cautioned against carrying firecrackers and other explosive materials on trains, as they could cause fires and explosions, endangering lives and railway property. They were informed about the provisions of Section 164 of the Railways Act, which prescribes imprisonment for up to three years for unauthorised possession or transportation of explosives on railway premises or trains. During the awareness drive, nine persons were apprehended for unauthorised trespassing and fined ₹500 each under Section 147 of the Railways Act, taking the total collection to ₹4,500. 62e36a797e1e03cf.title: Delivery firm employee arrested for stealing mobile phones
62e36a797e1e03cf.summary: Published - November 08, 2026 12:57 am IST - CHENNAI The Guindy police have arrested a 21-year-old employee of a private online delivery company for allegedly stealing two mobile phones from the firm’s returned goods inventory. Police said the complainant, Bhagavathi Murugan, 40, a resident of Guindy, works as a manager in the security and loss prevention department of a private online delivery company in the Guindy Industrial Estate. According to the complaint, Prathumna Krishna, an employee of the company, was responsible for inspecting goods returned by customers when deliveries could not be completed and processing them for return as per the prescribed procedures. When Bhagavathi Murugan recently checked the returned consignments, he found that two mobile phones received back on October 21 and 28, were missing. An internal check revealed that Krishna had allegedly stolen the phones. The police registered a case and examined CCTV footage and conducted inquiries at the company before arresting Prathumna Krishna, 21, a resident of Subramania Swamy Koil West Street, West Saidapet. Police recovered one mobile phone from him and ₹10,000, which he had allegedly obtained by selling the other stolen phone. 9256e15f091d794d.title: Centre allows transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh, other states
9256e15f091d794d.summary: The Centre has extended the Punjab Police and Correctional Services Act, 2006, to the Union Territory of Chandigarh, introducing provisions for the transfer of prisoners between states and Union territories and changes to the functioning of the prison administration. The notification, issued under Section 87 of the Punjab Reorganisation Act, 1966, extends the Punjab legislation to the Union Territory of Chandigarh with certain modifications, according to a notification issued by the Union Home Ministry on Friday. The amended provisions deal with the transfer of prisoners between Chandigarh and other states or Union territories. Under the provisions, prisoners serving sentences in Chandigarh, including life imprisonment, may be transferred to prisons in another state or Union territory with the consent of the government concerned and an order issued by the Chandigarh administrator. The amendments also provide for the transfer of undertrial prisoners in the interest of Chandigarh's .

09b406db0ac57bf2.title: Five killed, over a dozen injured as gunman opens fire in Poland's Krakow
09b406db0ac57bf2.summary: Five people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a market square in Krakow, Poland, police said. The gunman aimed at random people as he drove by the city's Main Square, Krakow police said. Police officers are among the wounded. The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a confrontation with police. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a post on X, said police are investigating the attack. Other details were not immediately available. Krakow is the second-largest city in Poland and roughly 250 kilometres from the capital, Warsaw.

8f2075cd50333015.title: UP govt hikes DA by 5%, employees to get arrears retrospectively from Jul 1
8f2075cd50333015.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has hiked the Dearness Allowance (DA) by 5 per cent for state government employees, staff in aided educational and technical institutions, regular and full-time employees of urban local bodies, work-charged employees, and those serving on UGC pay scales. Employees will now receive a Dearness Allowance of 63 per cent, up from 58 per cent. The increased rate will be effective from July 1, 2026, the state government said in a statement on Saturday. A government order was also issued in this regard on Saturday. The enhanced dearness allowance will be paid along with the regular salary for November 2026. This government decision will benefit lakhs of employees across the state. The move by the Yogi Adityanath government will provide relief not only to the state's regular employees but also to staff in aided educational institutions, urban local bodies, and other eligible categories of employees, the statement said.

0bd4985135c1371a.summary: As India and the US work to finalise a long-awaited trade deal, the ruling Republicans' major electoral loss in the recently concluded US midterm polls has raised crucial questions: How may this flip in the US Congress affect the India-US negotiations? Will the setback to US President Donald Trump's party give India room to negotiate? Experts believe that the Republican Party's stinging loss in the midterm elections, which shifted the balance of power in the US Congress , may push Trump to accelerate negotiations that had been reportedly stalled over tariff concerns. This, however, may not make the "US trade policy less restrictive", they said. Another expert explained why India may get some room to negotiate on “substance rather than under deadline pressure”. Professor Rituparna Kaushik, Assistant Professor at FLAME University, told Mint that the midterm election results will not rewrite US trade policy overnight. This is because "the Section 301 and Section 232 duties [under which tariffs were imposed] rest on executive authority and any rollback faces a presidential veto," he said. He believed that a Democratic Congress with oversight powers "makes abrupt tariff escalation politically harder, which gives India room to negotiate on substance rather than under deadline pressure". "Labour-intensive exporters in textiles, apparel, and gems and jewellery stand to gain most from that stability," he noted. On India’s strategy, Kaushik said New Delhi must "secure a predictable, rules-based tariff schedule rather than chase short-term concessions, and to broaden engagement beyond the White House to Congress and US states." "At the same time, India must keep diversifying through the EU agreement and other partners, so the US remains a key market but not a single point of vulnerability. On agriculture and dairy, India should hold firm, as US farm-lobby pressure cuts across party lines," he added. Ajay Srivastava, Founder of the Global Trade Research Initiative (GTRI), said

bbc6be00bd36b3cc.title: Investing in US stocks from India: Check how these 5 platforms stack up
bbc6be00bd36b3cc.summary: More Indian investors are buying US and other overseas stocks through apps and brokers. Indian investors who want US and other overseas stocks have more routes than ever. Mutual funds have hit the industry-wide $7 billion SEBI cap on overseas investments, so more investors are going direct under the RBI’s Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), which allows up to $250,000 per person a financial year. Demand is moving the market quickly. Platforms are adding features, changing how they are set up and launching products at pace, so it helps to know what each one does best and whether it fits your needs. This story looks at five: INDmoney, Interactive Brokers (IBKR), Vested Finance, Paasa and ZFunds. Business Standard heard from executives at four of the five and spoke to two investors who have used most of them. Four things separate these platforms. Notes: Vested charges $5 per USD withdrawal, which mainly applies to NRI accounts. “Size” figures are as reported by each company and are not like-for-like. Launched in 2019, INDmoney targets salaried retail investors and runs as an IFSCA-licensed Global Access Provider in GIFT City. It also files income tax returns for users, with Schedule FA filled in. The company reports $3.5 billion in global investing assets and plans to add European and Southeast Asian exchanges by December 2026. “We are not building a platform exclusively for wealthy individuals making large international remittances,” founder and CEO Ashish Kashyap told Business Standard . Founded in 1978, IBKR is a direct broker with no Indian intermediary and reported about 5.7 million client accounts in October 2026. It offers UCITS ETFs and several overseas markets, but has a complex interface, manual tax work and bank wire fees of ₹500–1,000 plus GST per transfer. Pranay Kapoor, a tech professional and YouTuber who has tried most of these apps, told Business Standard that with IBKR “there is no middleman.” Kapoor sends money in large tranches so the flat wire fee

6bb06909f49a0814.title: Book launched to honour work of child rights activist Thomas Jayaraj
6bb06909f49a0814.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:32 am IST - Chennai: The Centre for Child Rights and Development (CCRD) launched a book titled Voices of Transformation – Walking the path of Thomas Jayaraj towards a Culture of Child Rights to honour the contributions of Thomas Jayaraj, who passed away in 2021. He was at the forefront of many child rights initiatives at both the State and national levels. The book was released at the Madras School of Social Work (MSSW) on Friday by Sudha Ramalingam, senior advocate of Madras High Court. D. Geetha, Managing Trustee, CCRD, received the first copy. Stegana Jency L.T., Director of CCRD, said the team was committed to carrying forward the principles of Mr. Jayaraj. “We are launching this book because everything Mr. Jayaraj did should t become a guide for future leaders,” she said. Mr. Jayaraj’s daughter, Liby Rajam, said her father not only spoke for child rights, but also built a community that would continue to advocate for child rights in the future. Meanwhile, Ms. Ramalingam said there was considerable work to be done in this field. “When it comes to child rights and development, we must get the youngsters involved,” she said. Journalist and activist Aishwarya, and Antony Stephen, assistant professor and head of partnerships, MSSW, spoke about child rights advocacy. 450144925450d1cb.title: Centre orders rice stock disclosure, allows five states to impose limits
450144925450d1cb.summary: With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern states to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding. Under an order dated November 6, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all states and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories -- Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy. Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the food ministry said in a statement. Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka

b37d55aed236271b.summary: India's forex reserves dropped by USD 2.691 billion to USD 717.056 billion during the week ended October 30, the RBI said on Friday. In the previous week, the forex kitty had reduced by USD 1.269 billion to USD 719.748 billion. The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but have been on a decline ever since. Experts attribute this decline to the deployment of the FCNR(B) resources and also to currency defence put up by RBI through dollar sales. During the week ended October 30, foreign currency assets, a major component of reserves, decreased by USD 2.088 billion to USD 591.118 billion, according to the data released by Reserve Bank of India (RBI). d47a5aca9eff8a29.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 03:20 am IST - New Delhi Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement. | Photo Credit: M. Srinath With rice prices rising due to a deficient and uneven monsoon, the Centre on Friday (November 7, 2026) directed traders, retailers, wholesalers, processors and millers across the country to declare their rice and paddy stocks and allowed five southern States to impose stock limits to prevent hoarding. Under a November 6 order, all traders and wholesalers, retailers, large retail chains and processors and millers in all States and Union Territories must declare stocks under six categories — Basmati rice, non-Basmati premium rice, non-Basmati rice, parboiled rice, broken rice and paddy. Every unit holding stocks will have to update details on the Food Stock Portal (foodstock.dfpd.gov.in) every Friday, the Food Ministry said in a statement. Units that are not registered on the portal or that violate stock limits will face action under Sections 6 and 7 of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955. In a separate letter, also dated November 6, the Centre has given its consent to Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Telangana to impose stock limits on paddy and rice through control orders. The limits will remain in force till January 31, 2027. The Centre and States will monitor implementation to ensure adequate availability and prevent hoarding and black marketing, an official statement said. 0aa42e8c21ff097a.title: T.N. govt. allocates monthly maintenance fund of ₹1,000 to 12,646 VAO offices
0aa42e8c21ff097a.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:50 am IST - CHENNAI The Tamil Nadu government has issued an order allocating ₹1,000 each as a monthly maintenance fund to 12,646 Village Administrative Officer (VAO) offices functioning across the State, involving an annual expenditure of ₹15.18 crore. A Government Order to this effect was issued by the Revenue and Disaster Management Department on Friday. It follows an announcement made by Minister for Revenue and Disaster Management K.A. Sengottaiyan in the Assembly on August 17 during the Budget session. The maintenance fund will be used to arrange drinking water facilities, seating, ramps for persons with disabilities and other amenities for members of the public visiting VAO offices to obtain birth certificates, death certificates, patta, chitta, certificates for small and marginal farmers, legal heir certificates, income certificates, nativity certificates, community certificates and first-generation graduate certificates, among others. The monthly maintenance fund will be credited to the VAOs’ salaries under the head of maintenance allowance. The government has also allocated ₹8.85 crore towards this fund for the period from September 2026 to March 2027 in the current financial year. In an order issued on Friday, the State Government said considering the sensitive and complex nature of the cases, K.R. Sankaran, M. Sandhiya and Swami Subramanian were appointed as Special Public Prosecutors under Section 31(1) of the Act to conduct prosecution of the case investigated by the Special Investigation Team (SIT). Mr Veeramani and his associates are facing seven cases under the POCSO Act and one case of abetment to suicide of a minor in 2004. 23850def92ab4fc4.title: Agasthyamalai conservation case: SC directs temporary and non-resident silk cotton cultivators not eligible for protection under FRA Act
23850def92ab4fc4.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 01:47 am IST - NEW DELHI The Supreme Court directed on Friday that individuals with temporary residence in the Agasthyamalai biosphere or those living entirely outside the forest boundaries cannot be classified as traditional forest dwellers merely for cultivating silk cotton within the forest. “Persons falling in Category II and Category III, as classified in the additional affidavit of September 6 filed by Department of Revenue, State of Tamil Nadu, shall be excluded from consideration as forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers for the purposes of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 or FRA Act,” a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta directed. According to Tamil Nadu’s own affidavit, 232 persons are cultivating the forest area with temporary residence while 2,767 persons who occupy 2,867.70 hectares land are residing outside the forest boundary and are managing silk cotton cultivation. The order was passed in furtherance of a May 2026 judgment, which had issued various directions for a structured and time-bound process of eviction, rehabilitation and ecological restoration in the forest areas. The court had ordered the preparation of a division-wise eviction plan, removal of encroachments, and action against identified government servants. It had imposed a prohibition on approval or commencement of new non-forestry activities or diversion proposals within the Agasthyamalai landscape, and directed continued monitoring of the area by the Central Empowered Committee (CEC). Justice Mehta, who authored the order, held the State government “primarily responsible” for delaying the receipt of claims under the 2006 Act. 3254ea801e375485.title: Demonetisation and the health costs of cash shortages
3254ea801e375485.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST Liquidity is an economic determinant of health’ | Photo Credit: THE HINDU/MANJUNATH H.S. On November 8, 2016, 86% of India’s currency by value — in the form of ₹500 and ₹1,000 notes — ceased to be legal tender at just four hours’ notice. The stated objectives included curbing counterfeit currency and black money and accelerating the adoption of digital payments. It was among the largest transitory liquidity shocks engineered in a cash-reliant economy. Nearly all demonetised currency returned – some 99.3% as per Reserve Bank of India data – and broader financial indicators such as interest rates and deposits remained stable. As Chodorow-Reich et al. in their influential 2020 Quarterly Journal of Economics study have documented, the direct effect was a temporary reduction in the stock of money in the economy. 8da91880dd5ffb6b.title: Minister inaugurates dialysis centre
8da91880dd5ffb6b.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:35 am IST - CHENNAI Health Minister K.G. Arunraj inaugurated the “Rotary Kamdar Dialysis Centre” at the Government Peripheral Hospital in Anna Nagar on Friday. The centre, which was established by Rotary District 3234 in association with the Rotary Club of Chennai Kilpauk through a collaborative public-private partnership, aims at strengthening public healthcare infrastructure and improving access to essential dialysis services for patients requiring regular renal care. The initiative has been supported by the Pushpavati Babulal Kamdar Charitable Trust, Rotary Clubs of Chennai, and Wockhardt Foundation, in collaboration with Government Peripheral Hospital, Anna Nagar. The Rotary Clubs and Kamdar Charitable Trust have jointly provided medical equipment worth approximately ₹1.6 crore, including 10 dialysis machines, a Reverse Osmosis plant, and an effluent treatment plant. The centre is designed to serve up to 30 patients per day. The day-to-day dialysis expenses will be funded through the Chief Minister’s Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme, a press release said. Speaking at the inauguration, Dr. Arunraj said, “Healthcare is a shared responsibility, and it is important for all of us to contribute towards the well-being of society. The role played by Rotary in the eradication of polio is a wonderful example of what collective efforts and partnerships can achieve. We must build on this spirit of collaboration and work together towards our mission of eradicating cervical cancer.” The District Rotaract Council, Rotary International District 3234, in association with the Rotary Club of Chennai Kilpauk, also organised a Blood Donation Drive. D. Suresh Jain, District Governor 2026–27, Rotary International District 3234 and J.B. Kamdar, Managing Trustee, Pushpavati Babulal Kamdar Charitable Trust, were present. ecdfcae84b13fb27.title: Unhappy Milind Deora shoots a letter to BMC chief over event exclusion
ecdfcae84b13fb27.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 04:22 am IST - MUMBAI Shiv Sena MP Milind Deora. | Photo Credit: Emmanual Yogini Member of Parliament Milind Deora wrote a letter to Ashwini Bhide, Commissioner of the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC), on Friday regarding an omission. Mr. Deora stated that the BMC did not invite him to an inauguration in Colaba. Mr. Deora is a Rajya Sabha MP from the Shiv Sena, which is part of the ruling alliance in Maharashtra. Colaba falls in the area he represents. The event was for a housing project under the Ashray Yojana on November 6, 2026, with Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis and Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde attending. Speaker Rahul Narwekar, Mayor Ritu Tawde, and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi also attended. The BMC distributed keys to workers under the scheme. Mr. Deora wrote in the letter that representatives require notice of events in the areas they represent, noting that the event took place without informing him. He wrote that coordination and courtesy towards representatives must accompany initiatives, stating that representatives need to receive information about developments for the people they serve. The MP requested Mr. Bhide to look into the matter and asked the Commissioner to ensure that protocol is followed to prevent an omission. He requested that officials receive advice to ensure coordination with representatives for functions. 04b27ca4a8352a99.title: Supreme Court decision on BBMB arrears a victory for Himachal, says CM Sukhu
04b27ca4a8352a99.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 01:30 am IST - New Delhi Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu. | Photo Credit: ANI Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday (November 6, 2026) termed the Supreme Court’s decision directing Punjab and Haryana to supply 11,973 million units of electricity to the State over 20 years towards its outstanding dues from the Bhakra-Nangal and Beas hydroelectric projects a historic victory for its people. The order settles a decades-old dispute over Himachal Pradesh’s 7.19% share in the power generated from the projects. The State will receive nearly 60 crore units annually during the lean season, generating an estimated revenue of ₹10,000 crore to ₹20,000 crore over the 20-year period, depending on electricity prices, Mr. Sukhu said in a statement. He said the decision could fetch the State additional revenue of up to ₹1,000 crore annually. Even at ₹6 per unit, Himachal Pradesh would earn at least ₹500 crore a year, while a rate of ₹13-14 per unit would significantly increase the returns. Mr. Sukhu attributed the outcome to the State government’s sustained legal battle and determination to secure its financial rights. He described it as the fourth major success in protecting Himachal Pradesh’s interests, citing earlier victories in matters relating to Wildflower Hall, the Kishau Dam among others. The Chief Minister said the government was also pursuing its claims over the Shanan Power Project and the water cess. The additional revenue, he said, would be used to strengthen education and healthcare, improve road infrastructure, generate employment and ensure timely payment of financial benefits to government employees. Congratulating the State’s nearly 75 lakh residents, Mr. Sukhu said protecting its resources and making Himachal Pradesh self-reliant remained a top priority for his government. cee9fdc5046b6afa.title: Rural women narrate stories on how Gruha Lakshmi scheme helped build their lives
cee9fdc5046b6afa.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:07 am IST - Bengaluru Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar admiring a handmade beaded toy cradle gifted by one of the beneficiaries of the Gruha Lakshmi scheme at his home office in Bengaluru on Friday. | Photo Credit: ANI Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar’s interaction with Gruha Lakshmi scheme beneficiaries in Bengaluru on Friday turned out to be a forum for hearing stories about how the monthly cash deposit by the scheme helped poor women not just build their lives, but also make significant achievements like helping their wards pursue higher education. At the interaction, which was held at the Chief Minister’s home office to get feedback from beneficiaries on the occasion of the scheme completing three years of implementation, a woman from Chikkamagaluru district said: “My son is studying MBBS in Koppal. 7873579ddeec35fd.title: Governor asks for status report on all public universities in Karnataka
7873579ddeec35fd.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:55 am IST - Bengaluru Sudha Yadav, Governor of Karnataka and Chancellor of universities in the State, directed all public universities in the State to conduct a comprehensive review of their current operations and identify areas requiring improvement. The Governor instructed all Vice-Chancellors to prepare and submit a detailed report on the same. “This report should cover the current status of their respective universities, key achievements, challenges, shortcomings, and specific measures proposed for improvement,” she stated. Addressing the Vice-Chancellors of various universities and officials from the Karnataka State Higher Education Council at Lok Bhavan, the Governor emphasised the need to strengthen the quality, transparency, accountability and overall performance of universities across the State. “Emphasis must be placed on the effective implementation of the National Education Policy and the State Education Policy, strong coordination between industries and universities, as well as skill development, research, innovation and employability,” she said. The Governor called upon all Vice-Chancellors and the Karnataka State Higher Education Council to work in coordination and collaboration to strengthen the higher education system in Karnataka. 5160f15808b589f8.title: Krishi mela will be held for three days instead of one day: Agriculture Minister
5160f15808b589f8.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST - Bengaluru Agriculture Minister P.M. Narendraswamy | Photo Credit: File Photo Krishi mela will be held for three days instead of one day, as was was announced earlier. Agriculture Minister P. M. Narendraswamy on Friday said that krishi mela at the Gandhi Krishi Vignana Kendra (GKVK) in Bengaluru will be held for three days this year as well. “Given the drought conditions prevailing in the State, there had been discussions about limiting the Mela to a single day. However, the event will continue for three days, just as in previous years,” he said. The three days event will proceed to introduce farmers to agricultural innovations and drought-management strategies, despite the current drought situation. He further noted that a three-day krishi mela will be also held in Mandya. “Three-day krishi mela have already been organised at the Universities of Agriculture Sciences in Shivamogga and Dharwad. These events have provided thousands of farmers with information on new crop varieties and technologies, as well as methods for managing drought,” he said. f6f0dde8fcb3adfd.title: Delhi court rejects plea seeking FIR against CM for comparing govt officials to Lord Hanuman
f6f0dde8fcb3adfd.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 04:30 am IST New Delhi, Nov 04 (ANI): Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta speaks during a fireside chat on 'Rooftop Solar as a Catalyst for Global Energy Transition' at the Solar Plenary Session of the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit and Expo 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, in New Delhi on Wednesday. (ANI Photo/Sumit) | Photo Credit: ANI A Delhi court on Friday dismissed a complaint seeking legal action against Chief Minister Rekha Gupta over her alleged remarks comparing government officials to Lord Hanuman during an official event. Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Ashwani Panwar of the Rouse Avenue Courts dismissed the complaint filed by Ram Niwas Sharma. In his complaint, Mr. Sharma alleged that Ms. Gupta, while addressing an event on September 23, 2025, compared Delhi government officials to Hanuman, saying they recognised their authority only when confronted with a situation similar to having their “tails set on fire”. He further alleged that Ms. Gupta referred to Hanuman in the context of the programme being organised near the shrine of Marghat Wale Baba in Kashmere Gate. The remarks were reportedly made during the launch of an interstate Delhi Transport Corporation bus service connecting Delhi with Baraut in Uttar Pradesh. Claiming that the remarks had hurt his religious sentiments, Mr. Sharma sought directions from the court for registration of an FIR and appropriate legal action against the Chief Minister. Last month, the court had sought a response from the Delhi Police on the complaint. In its Action Taken Report (ATR), the police stated that the alleged remarks did not disclose the commission of any cognizable offence. It maintained that Ms. Gupta’s speech, when viewed in its entirety, reflected appreciation for government employees and expressed reverence towards the Hindu deity. 7a7674b95a48cf58.title: Ahead of Deepavali, 3 major blazes erupt in Capital; DFS on alert
7a7674b95a48cf58.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:54 am IST A major fire broke out at a four-storey commercial building in Delhi's Gaffar Market in the early hours of Friday (November 6, 2026), just days before Deepavali and on the occasion of Dhanteras, triggering a massive emergency response. Around 20-25 fire engines were rushed to the spot to bring the blaze under control. No casualties or injuries have been reported. | Photo Credit: Sushil Kumar Verma The Delhi Fire Services (DFS) received 78 calls about fire incidents between midnight and 7.30 p.m. on Friday, including three major fires at commercial establishments across the Capital that required large-scale firefighting operations involving more than 20 fire tenders each. At least 15 people were rescued and seven injuries were reported, officials said. The DFS has issued a high alert and cancelled the leave of its officers and staff amid the increased fire risk ahead of Deepavali on Sunday. In Gali No. 6 of Gandhi Nagar’s Shanti Mohalla, the blaze gutted a ground-plus-four-storey garment warehouse. Assistant Divisional Officer Santosh Kumar said, “Four hose lines were laid from different directions to reach the building while the fire tender remained stationed on the main road.” A local resident said a suspected short circuit caused the fire. In Karol Bagh’s Gaffar Market, fire engulfed a commercial complex housing around 50 mobile accessories shops across its basement, ground floor, three upper floors, and a tin shed on the terrace. “The absence of ventilation led to smoke accumulating inside the building, making it difficult for firefighters to access the premises. There were no firefighting arrangements inside the shops and godowns,” Deputy Chief Fire Officer M.K. Chattopadhyay, who oversaw the operation, said. At a car showroom near the Saket metro station, at least 12-15 people were rescued from the top of the building and another four from its rear. Seven persons sustained injuries and were taken to hospital, police said

df43ab4012430c6d.title: University of Madras, Sutherland Global Services to collaborate for setting up an AI lab
df43ab4012430c6d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:49 am IST - Chennai The Syndicate of University of Madras (UoM) on Friday approved a proposal to sign a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Sutherland Global Services, a digital-driven business transformation company, to set up an AI laboratory at the Department of Women Studies. The company has offered to upgrade its older allocation of ₹50 lakh for a Gender Lab that was set up at the Department following an older MoU signed in April 2019. The lab offered an online course on Gender Sensitisation and Workplace Readiness to students across the four campuses of the University. However, the lockdown led to long closure of the lab that destroyed the digital equipment. The company has now come forward to renew the MoU and upgrade the lab installing new systems and infrastructure. In addition to reviving the Gender Lab, the MoU seeks to establish an Artificial Intelligence Lab for Inclusive Education that would develop e-modules for a course on Application of Artificial Intelligence. The Syndicate also cleared a few long-pending issues that have been holding up recruitment of faculty members to various Arts and Science self-financing colleges and government-aided colleges (self financing courses). The apex body has approved resumption of special drives at the University to grant approval of qualifications to Assistant Professors for the current academic year. University records indicated that it had received about 400 proposals from various affiliated colleges seeking approval of qualification of the faculty members appointed in those colleges. The Syndicate also approved the appointment of principals to Agurchand Manmull Jain College, Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College, Shrimathi Devkunvar Nanalal Bhatt Vaishnav College for Women, Sir Theagaraya College, and Madras School of Social Work. 278fb4dc962bb62f.title: Avadi, Tambaram police destroy over 1.7 tonnes of ganja
278fb4dc962bb62f.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:33 am IST The Avadi and Tambaram City Police on Friday destroyed over 1.7 tonnes of ganja, besides narcotic tablets, heroin, methamphetamine, ganja chocolates, and gutkha products seized in various cases. The Avadi City Police destroyed 906.654 kg of ganja, 3,820 narcotic tablets, 10 ganja chocolates, and 2,685 kg of gutkha and other tobacco products, seized in 190 cases registered across the Commissionerate limits. A committee comprising Joint Commissioner R. Sivakumar, Deputy Commissioner V. Vinodh Santharam, and Assistant Director of Forensic Sciences Vijayalakshmi oversaw the process. The contraband was incinerated at an authorised facility at Thenmelpakkam in Chengalpattu district, following court orders. Meanwhile, the Tambaram City Police destroyed 810 kg of ganja, 0.148 g of heroin, 0.961 g of methamphetamine and 6,610 narcotic tablets seized in various cases. Joint Commissioner R. Jayanthi and Deputy Commissioner K. Karthikeyan supervised the process. With Friday’s destruction, the Tambaram police have destroyed 4,774 kg of ganja since 2025. The disposal was carried out in accordance with the procedures prescribed under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985, the police said. 25f8461565d6fe44.title: WTA Chennai Open: Montgomery snaps Maaya’s memorable run, Indian challenge ends
25f8461565d6fe44.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:15 am IST - CHENNAI Robin Montgomery overcame a slow start to beat Maaya | Photo Credit: R. RAGU Robin Montgomery overcame an early setback to defeat wild card Maaya Rajeshwaran 6-3, 6-3 in the quarterfinals, ending the Indian challenge in singles at the WTA 250 Chennai Open on Friday. The 17-year-old Maaya - the first Indian woman to feature in the last-eight stage of a Tour-level event since Sania Mirza in Pattaya City in 2012 - was particularly impressive in the early stages. She tried to handle the 5’10” tall American’s lefty serve, which averaged above the 180km/h mark, by constantly adjusting her position near the baseline. The Indian got the early break in the fifth game of the opener courtesy a netted backhand from World No. 151 Montgomery, much to the delight of the 500-odd spectators under the floodlights on Centre Court at the SDAT Stadium in Nungambakkam here. But when it came to consolidating the break, the girl from Coimbatore, who had been landing plenty of first serves in the high 170s range, couldn’t find one till she was 15-30 down. Montgomery converted her first opportunity to restore parity. Maaya also let the eighth game - in which she committed two double faults - slip after being 40-30 up and was broken again. The 22-year-old Montgomery, former World No. 95, served the first set out. In the second essay, the American was in control as she earned the double break advantage at 4-1. After Maaya retrieved one of them back, Montgomery held quickly for a 5-3 lead and finished the job with a crosscourt backhand winner to break the Indian for the third time in the set. 81e8cbc939bfd5a6.title: NU observes BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week with anti-plastic programme
81e8cbc939bfd5a6.summary: Lumami, November 6 (MExN): Nagaland University (NU) organised a special programme on “Say No to Single-Use Plastics” on November 5 as part of the BRICS Sustainable Lifestyle Week (BSLW), being observed from November 1 to 7. The programme was held at the Conference Hall of the Department of Environmental Science (EVS) and commenced with a welcome address by Dr Latonglila Jamir, Head of the Department of EVS and member of the Committee for MISSION LiFE.This was followed by a brief introduction to the programme by Peter Ki, Public Relations Officer, who highlighted the alignment between India's 2026 BRICS Chairship, with its focus on sustainability, and the objectives of Mission LiFE.Delivering a lecture, Dr Jamir discussed the origins and environmental impact of single-use plastics, attributing the growing crisis to the demand for convenience and the widespread use of disposable packaging and products that require no cleaning, storage or maintenance. She pointed out that plastics designed for use over a few minutes can persist in the environment for centuries, creating serious ecological imbalances. Their toxic impacts extend across their entire life cycle, from petrochemical extraction and manufacturing to consumption and eventual waste disposal. Tracing the historical development of plastic use, she said its consumption increased sharply in the early 1950s and expanded further through the 1990s. Although environmental awareness emerged during the 1960s and 1970s, followed by extensive research into the 2010s, effective bans gained momentum only after 2018. She also outlined the seven main categories of plastics: polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), polyvinyl chloride (PVC), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polypropylene (PP), polystyrene (PS) and others. Highlighting the scale of the problem, Dr Jamir said approximately 400 million metric tonnes of plastic waste are generated globally every year, with half comprising single-use items.

0c399e4392ad7695.title: Bharti Airtel reclaims 2nd spot in mcap rankings, overtakes Jio Platforms
0c399e4392ad7695.summary: Bharti Airtel on Friday reclaimed the title of the country's second most valuable company by market valuation, overtaking Jio Platforms. At market close, Bharti Airtel shares ended 1.66 per cent higher at Rs 2,096.25 on the BSE. During the day, the stock climbed 2.81 per cent to Rs 2,120. However, the stock of Jio Platforms dipped 0.90 per cent to end at Rs 1,405.75. Intraday, it declined 2 per cent to Rs 1,390. The market valuation of Bharti Airtel stood at Rs 13 lakh crore, while that of Jio Platforms was Rs 12.94 lakh crore. Jio Platforms Ltd, the Reliance Industries-backed digital services company, on October 28 became the second most valuable Indian company by market valuation following an impressive debut on the Dalal Street. Reliance Industries continues to remain the most valued domestic firm, with a market valuation of Rs 17,83,723.93 crore. 9a1e90c5c82cee07.title: Police conduct raids at 14 hookah bars; book 13 for violations
9a1e90c5c82cee07.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:31 am IST The Greater Chennai Police (GCP), in coordination with the Health Department, on Thursday conducted surprise inspections at 14 hookah bars operating in the city, to curb the use of banned tobacco products and narcotic substances. The joint inspection teams carried out raids at hookah bars in Teynampet, Vepery, Nungambakkam, Egmore, Anna Salai, Mylapore, and Royapettah. During the inspections, officers checked whether the establishments operated with valid licences, complied with government regulations, and allowed the use of banned narcotic substances. Based on suspicions of violations, the police registered cases against those operating 13 of the 14 hookah bars inspected. Materials used for smoking hookah were seized from the establishments. The seized items will be sent to the forensic science laboratory for examination, the police said. GCP Commissioner A. Amalraj has advised the public, particularly youngsters, to refrain from using banned tobacco products and narcotic substances that can adversely affect their health. The police have warned that surprise inspections will continue in coordination with the Health Department, and that appropriate legal action will be initiated against hookah bars found operating illegally or permitting the use of banned substances. Shivakumar on Friday alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take credit for Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Bengaluru on November 13 to inaugurate the metro Pink Line, even though he was arriving on the official invitation of the State government. Without taking the name of BJP MP Tejasvi Surya, the Chief Minister alleged that some BJP leaders were trying to take publicity by claiming that they were responsible for the Prime Minsiter’s proposed visit. Speaking to media persons in Kanakapura, he wondered why the BJP leaders were tying to take publicity for this event though they had nothing to do with it. “We are developing metro network by borrowing money. 88705d48441c9095.title: Isolated rain likely in Andhra Pradesh till November 12
88705d48441c9095.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:11 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM Isolated rain was recorded over Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam, and Rayalaseema in the 24 hours ending 8.30 a.m. on Friday (November 6, 2026), the Meteorological Centre, Amaravati, said. The northeast monsoon remained normal, with no heat wave or heavy rainfall. Komarada in Parvathipuram Manyam received 50 mm, followed by Nellore 44 mm, and Madanapalle 33.4 mm. An upper-air cyclonic circulation persists over east Telangana and adjoining Coastal Andhra Pradesh. Thunderstorms with lightning and winds of 30-40 kmph, gusting to 50 kmph, are likely at one or two places along the coast till November 9. Isolated light to moderate rain is forecast State-wide till November 12. Kurnool recorded the day’s highest maximum temperature 36°C, which was 4°C above normal. Visakhapatnam recorded 32.3°C, 1.5°C above normal, and Amaravati 33.7°C. Tirupati received 5 mm and Bapatla 4 mm of rain later on Friday. Since October 1, the State has received 191.1 mm against a normal of 194 mm, with Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam 20% above normal and Rayalaseema 33% below. P.L.N. Murthy, Head, Cyclone Warning Centre, Visakhapatnam, said the Extended Range Outlook indicated an upper-air circulation over the southeast Bay of Bengal around November 11. Under its influence, a low-pressure area was likely to form in the same region around November 13 or 14, with no probability of further intensification as of now. ab0926045c5e10a8.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:10 am IST - Coimbatore The Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore has not withdrawn any of the books supplied by Agal Vilakku Pathipagam, whose publications have come under scrutiny following allegations of irregularities in the procurement of books. V. Santhanakrishnan, in-charge librarian of Periyar Arivulagam, told The Hindu on Friday that publications from Agal Vilakku Pathipagam were being kept in a separate rack in the library. “We have not withdrawn any of those books so far. We have also not received any communication from our department regarding the issue,” he said. This comes after Tamil writer Perumal Murugan flagged alleged inaccuracies and questionable authorship in several of the books displayed at the library. He had pointed out that Agal Vilakku Pathipagam had supplied around 1,800 titles to the library. 3026f9d08605b6d4.title: Stakeholders oppose Karnataka govt.’s move to make private schools adopt govt. schools
3026f9d08605b6d4.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:07 am IST - Bengaluru The Save Public Education Committee and the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) termed the initiative an attempt by the State government to shut down government schools. Educationalists, student organisations, academicians, teachers and other stakeholders have criticised the State government’s plan to link government schools with private schools through adoption. Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar recently held a meeting with private schools and companies, where he proposed the adoption of government schools by private schools and other firms under Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) funds. The Save Public Education Committee and the All India Democratic Students’ Organisation (AIDSO) termed the initiative an attempt by the State government to shut down government schools. “We strongly condemn this anti-people move. The government has allowed private schools to even tag their names to adopted government schools. By doing this, the government is trying to escape its responsibility to address the deficiencies in the public education system,” the committee said. The committee also condemned remarks allegedly made by representatives of private schools at the meeting against government school teachers, including by Aishwarya DKS Hegde, daughter of Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and Trustee Secretary of the National Education Foundation. “During the interaction, they said the quality of teachers in government schools is low. They shifted the entire blame onto teachers while ignoring the role of the government’s own policies in creating the situation,” the committee said. Meanwhile, teachers have expressed displeasure over the remarks. “Teachers are burdened with non-academic work. For example, this year we were deputed for Special Intensive Revision (SIR) work. bab4009692b2411d.title: Deepavali: light up inner self
bab4009692b2411d.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 05:04 am IST Scriptures say when one surrenders to Perumal in all humility, He negates all the negative actions of one until that time. Festivals celebrating the fall of asuras and their subsequent liberation illustrate this aspect admirably. Many asuras undertook severe penance and prayed to the Almighty seeking boons, which finally were the catalyst to their downfall. Dharma will always prevail, as will total surrender to God without seeking anything in return, an aspect underscored in the Bhagavad Gita. Deepavali, the festival of lights celebrating the fall of the Narakasura underscores this perfectly, said Damal S. Ramakrishnan. Deepavali is a festival of lights, not merely of the exterior landscape, but more importantly of one’s inner self. The legend of Narakasura is a well-known one. Born as the son of Bhoo Devi, Narakasura undertook severe penance and was granted the boon that he sought, which was that none barring his mother could kill him. Like most asuras, after gaining the boon, he unleashed a series of atrocities that affected all living things. Lord Krishna took on the asura in a fierce bout, but the power of the boon held and Krishna fell faint in the chariot. His Consort Satyabhama took charge of the situation and wounded him mortally. She was none other than Bhoo Devi, who had manifested as Satyabhama when Perumal descended to earth as Krishna. In the time between his fall and death, the asura realised his folly and becoming truly repentant for his sins, sought another boon: His death should be celebrated in a grand manner by mankind as a reminder that only virtue will prevail and will be truly rewarded. On this day the goddesses too help one light up one’s inner self. Ganga, the purifier of one’s sins, flows into all the waterways. It is customary to have oil bath early in the morning of Deepavali and greet one another with the query, “Is Ganga snan over?” as a way of indicating that one should get rid of one’s sins. G

9ce11902c8b76033.title: Duraimurugan clarifies on Hindu rituals at granddaughter’s wedding
9ce11902c8b76033.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:38 am IST - Chennai Under fire from the Dravidar Kazhagam and its affiliates for conducting his granddaughter’s wedding with traditional Hindi rituals recently, DMK general secretary Duraimurugan on Friday said it was done as per her wishes. Clarifying his stance amid the backlash, Mr Duraimurugan in a statement said: “My granddaughter, educated overseas, shared with me that she was in love with an individual outside our caste and wished to marry him with traditional Hindu rituals. The ceremony was held entirely at her request. I conceded to the arrangement only due to her strong persistence. I express my regret over this development and request everyone not to make it a political issue or a subject of debate”. 283d7fb296225f60.title: Amid the sparkle of Deepavali, ophthalmologists sound a note of caution
283d7fb296225f60.summary: Published - November 07, 2026 12:39 am IST - CHENNAI The sound of firecrackers is not far away, with Deepavali drawing closer. But the excitement of bursting crackers comes with a word of caution from ophthalmologists, as they warn that a moment of carelessness could cause eye injuries ranging from minor abrasions to severe ocular trauma. M. Elangovan, Director, Regional Institute of Ophthalmology and Government Ophthalmic Hospital, said there are different types of crackers. “Bursting types (explosive crackers) will produce irregular, small, and forcible particles in all directions, and are the most dangerous. These particles travel at such a velocity that they could hit or penetrate any soft surface. Then, there is the direct heat injury caused by crackers such as sparklers that result in scars in the cornea or conjunctiva due to the heat generated. Sudden and close exposure to bright light-emitting crackers can also cause bleaching or temporary blackout due to the impact on the rod and cone cells in the retina,” he said. G. Suganeswari, Senior Vitreo Retina Consultant, Sankara Nethralaya, said, “Cracker-related eye injuries can include chemical burns, thermal injuries, and injuries caused by foreign bodies, with the damage ranging from superficial injuries to deeper involvement of the most vital structures of the eye. Any structure of the eye, starting from eyelids, conjunctiva, cornea, lens, retina, and optic nerve, are prone to injuries caused by crackers. There can be open wounds that need immediate attention. These injuries have a prolonged course of recovery, and can also be potentially blinding.” T.S. Surendran, chairman, Sankara Nethralaya, said that last year, the hospital saw several patients with smoke-related injuries, chemical burns, foreign body lodgement, rupture globe, retinal trauma, and internal eye bleeding during Deepavali. 8317c1d66e3d9652.title: Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services gears up for Deepavali
8317c1d66e3d9652.summary: Updated - November 07, 2026 12:40 am IST Areas such as T. Nagar, Purasawalkam, Parry’s Corner, George Town, Washermenpet, Royapuram, Triplicane, Mylapore, Anna Nagar, Koyambedu, Ambattur and Tambaram will receive particular attention. The Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services (TNFRS) has strengthened its fire prevention, emergency response and rescue preparedness across the Chennai Northern Region in view of the forthcoming Deepavali festival, when the extensive use of fireworks, increased commercial activity and large public gatherings pose heightened fire safety challenges. G. Sathiyanarayan, Additional Director of TNFRS said the additional deployment would supplement the Northern Region’s existing strength of 813 personnel and 136 vehicles, taking the total available manpower to 1,129 and the fleet to 158 vehicles. The arrangements cover four fire service districts — Chennai South, Chennai North, Chennai Central and Chennai Suburban — with special focus on densely populated residential neighbourhoods, commercial establishments, fireworks outlets, crowded market streets and other vulnerable locations. The existing fleet includes water tenders, quick response vehicles, water bowsers, foam tenders, emergency rescue vehicles and Bronto Skylifts. The additional vehicles will be strategically positioned based on local risk assessments to ensure quicker response to emergencies, particularly in congested localities where access for large firefighting vehicles could be difficult. Areas such as T. Nagar, Purasawalkam, Parry’s Corner, George Town, Washermenpet, Royapuram, Triplicane, Mylapore, Anna Nagar, Koyambedu, Ambattur and Tambaram will receive particular attention. 5c17017b0409d18f.title: Bombay HC, Mahalaxmi Racecourse and Amitabh Bachchan's residence receive bomb threat email
5c17017b0409d18f.summary: A bomb threat email sent to the Bombay High Court also threatened the Bombay Stock Exchange, Mahalaxmi Racecourse and actor Amitabh Bachchan's residence, Jalsa, triggering a security alert in Mumbai, NDTV reported. Police and security agencies are investigating the email to identify the sender. Amitabh Bachchan had received a similar threat email earlier on October 23. The message, which was also sent to Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi, warned of a grenade attack at a school on October 31 and threatened to target the actor’s Juhu residence between October 31 and November 27. The email had claimed that a blast would take place in the mayor's office at the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) headquarters. The premises were searched, but nothing suspicious was found. The email, which made a references to ‘Khalistan’, also threatened an attack during singer Diljit Dosanjh’s November 27 concert in the Mahalaxmi Racecourse area. Following the threat, the 84-year-old actor changed his customary Sunday interaction with fans outside his residence. Bachchan greeted the gathering from behind a transparent bulletproof enclosure installed on an elevated platform. His son, actor Abhishek Bachchan, and several security personnel were also present as he waved to fans from behind the protective glass. The district and sessions courts in Maharashtra's Pune, Thane, Hingoli, Beed, and Nanded received emails threatening bomb blasts on the premises on November 2, triggering a security scare and a police search. Police said nothing suspicious was found during searches. According to police, the court building in Thane city was evacuated in the afternoon as the office received a message that a bomb would explode at 3.30 pm. "Personnel from Thane Nagar police station evacuated the entire court complex. Judges, advocates and other staffers were safely led out of the premises. A dog squad and BDDS personnel then carried out a thorough search," an official was quoted

Police and security agencies are investigating the email to identify the sender. Amitabh Bachchan had received a similar threat email earlier on October 23. The message, which was also sent to Mumbai Mayor Ritu Tawde and Deputy Mayor Sanjay Ghadi, warned of a grenade attack at a school on October 31 and threatened to target the actor’s Juhu residence between October 31 and November 27. The email had claimed that a blast would take place in the mayor's office at the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) headquarters. The premises were searched, but nothing suspicious was found. The email, which made a references to ‘Khalistan’, also threatened an attack during singer Diljit Dosanjh’s November 27 concert in the Mahalaxmi Racecourse area. Following the threat, the 84-year-old actor changed his customary Sunday interaction with fans outside his residence. Bachchan greeted the gathering from behind a transparent bulletproof enclosure installed on an elevated platform. His son, actor Abhishek Bachchan, and several security personnel were also present as he waved to fans from behind the protective glass. The district and sessions courts in Maharashtra's Pune, Thane, Hingoli, Beed, and Nanded received emails threatening bomb blasts on the premises on November 2, triggering a security scare and a police search. Police said nothing suspicious was found during searches. According to police, the court building in Thane city was evacuated in the afternoon as the office received a message that a bomb would explode at 3.30 pm. "Personnel from Thane Nagar police station evacuated the entire court complex. Judges, advocates and other staffers were safely led out of the premises. A dog squad and BDDS personnel then carried out a thorough search," an official was quoted
