b60989953528667d.title: India opens deepwater oil, gas bids, offers to fund up to 50% of well costs
b60989953528667d.summary: The government is rolling out a special licensing round for deepwater and ultra-deepwater oil and gas blocks, offering monthly bidding windows and relaxed fiscal terms as it prepares to shoulder up to 50 per cent of eligible exploratory well costs under its Rs 84,084-crore Samudra Manthan offshore exploration programme. The special round under the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) is aimed at accelerating exploration in India's offshore frontier basins by lowering entry barriers, sharing the high costs and risks of deepwater drilling, and making acreage available to investors throughout the year. "Under the government's 'Samudra Manthan' National Offshore Exploration Scheme, a Special OALP is being introduced for fast-track award of deepwater and ultra-deepwater (DW/UDW) exploration blocks," the Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) said in a notice. DGH said details of the bid round will be announced shortly. The Special OALP is a key licensing and investment facilitation .

672443eac83c9dae.title: ₹170 crore theft over 10 years: Woman spends employer’s money on Rolex watches, private jets, luxury handbags
672443eac83c9dae.summary: A 47-year-old woman in California has admitted to defrauding her employer of almost $18 million ( approximately ₹ 170 crore) over a period of 10 years, using the stolen money to finance an extravagant lifestyle involving luxury shopping, private jet journeys, and expensive home renovations. Lizbeth Sherman, a resident of El Dorado Hills, pleaded guilty to federal wire fraud charges on Monday, according to the US Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of California. The woman spent the money on designer handbags, Rolex watches, luxury holidays and other high-value purchases. Sherman's alleged fraud began in 2015 when she took up a position as an executive assistant to a retired venture capitalist from the San Francisco Bay Area. As part of her responsibilities, she was given access to her employer's bank account to manage credit card payments. However, she gradually misused this access to divert large sums of money towards her personal expenses. Between September 2015 and May 2025, she repeatedly transferred funds to cover her own credit card bills, prosecutors said. “Between September 2015 and May 2025, Sherman abused this access and stole nearly $18 million from her employer in order to pay off her own extravagant credit card expenses,” federal prosecutors said. The stolen money enabled Sherman to make expensive purchases and maintain a lavish lifestyle for years. Her spending reportedly included designer handbags from Louis Vuitton, luxury watches, expensive holidays and private jet journeys. She also spent a substantial amount on vehicles and renovations to her $2 million home in El Dorado Hills. “In this manner, Sherman spent tens of thousands of dollars on luxury handbags, Rolex watches, resort-level vacations, private jet travel, vehicles, and improvements to a $2 million residence in El Dorado Hills.” Over time, Sherman also began selling some of the luxury products she had purchased using her employer's money through online marketplaces. faf451da2645dd68.title: Danger in the sewer: On India’s sewer cleaning deaths
faf451da2645dd68.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 01:36 am IST Despite legislation, Supreme Court orders, government programmes, the availability of mechanised cleaning technologies, and exhortations from politicians, India continues to lose sanitation workers to foreseeable, and largely preventable, circumstances. In a recent incident, four workers lost their lives in Ujjain, Madhya Pradesh , cleaning a hotel’s food-waste chamber. According to Parliament and the National Commission for Safai Karamcharis data, the number of workers who died on jobs involving sewer and septic tanks was 859 between 2014 and 2025, 498 from 2019 to mid-2026, 332 across 18 States and Union Territories in 2021-26, and 1,350 between 1993 and 2025. The figures have never tended towards zero even as the Safai Karamchari Andolan has repeatedly alleged severe under-reporting. Further, the government has maintained since at least 2021 that the practice of manually cleaning excreta from insanitary latrines has been eliminated, effectively signalling that it believes it has addressed the root of the problem when it has not, and freeing administrative bodies of the urgency of inspecting municipalities and private establishments. Members of historically marginalised castes are also overrepresented in these jobs. The law has distinguished hazardous cleaning of sewers and septic tanks from manual scavenging since 2013. Even so, persons entering them are still vulnerable to noxious gases. In Dr. Balram Singh (2023), the Court strengthened the requirements under Safai Karamchari Andolan (2014) to, among other measures, ensure outsourced sewer-cleaning contracts did not entail workers entering sewers and raise the compensation for deaths to ₹30 lakh per worker. 434704210c1cb0d2.title: The ecological fallout of Israel’s war in Gaza
434704210c1cb0d2.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 01:56 am IST ‘The UNEP report does not capture the full extent of the environmental devastation in Gaza, as the situation continues to deteriorate’ | Photo Credit: AFP On November 5, 2001, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) designated November 6 each year as the International Day for Preventing the Exploitation of the Environment in War and Armed Conflict . This recognition underscores the far-reaching impacts of environmental damage caused by armed conflict, including degradation of ecosystems and resource depletion well after the conflict period. This impact often extends beyond the limits of national territories and affects future generations. Considering the importance of the issue, the International Law Commission (ILC), in its report titled ‘Protection of the Environment in Relation to Armed Conflicts’ (PERAC), adopted 27 draft principles in 2022, which were formally noted by the UNGA on December 7, 2022. The overarching purpose of these principles is to enhance the protection of the environment in relation to armed conflicts. The first principle of the PERAC provides that the principles apply to the protection of the environment before, during and after an armed conflict, including in situations of occupation. In this context, Israel’s responsibility for internationally wrongful acts causing environmental harm arises not only from its ongoing genocide in Gaza but also from its continuing role as an occupying power. 104d6ee3391cce6a.title: Fifty years ago | Good scope for Indo-British ventures
104d6ee3391cce6a.summary: Published - November 06, 2026 02:29 am IST Bombay, November 5: Britain and India could collaborate in many industrial fields particularly off-shore oil drilling and electronics, Sir Ralph Bateman, leader of the British industrial co-operation mission, told pressmen here on Wednesday. Britain’s expert management and sound technology would match well with Indian administrative and technical skill. The two countries could help each other by matching their high level attainments in various fields of industrial activity in the interests of both the countries. Sir Ralph said just because British’s financial conditions were not rosy, one should not jump to the conclusion that it would not be in a position to help others. All the developed countries tend to work together and they tried to co-operate with each other in the advancement of industrial progress. Sir Ralph said in reply to a question that troubles in U.K. were mainly political and not industrial. He wanted the public expenditure in his country to be cut. They were spending too much on many heads and this should be stopped. Asked whether he was satisfied with the Indian Government’s policy on repatriation of dividends etc. he said they had no complaints to make. 75899e9c71a95989.title: Deafblind persons urge government to include them separately in Census 2027
75899e9c71a95989.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:26 am IST - Chennai Persons with deafblindness on Thursday urged the Union government to count their disability separately in Census 2027, as they require the count for making policy decisions . Addressing the media, Syed Ali Fathima, who is deafblind, said, “It will benefit us if we are counted separately in Census 2027. Various needs of our community remain unaddressed, beginning with job opportunities. When we can determine the exact number of people with this disability, policy changes can be made to benefit us.” Deafblindness is a combination of hearing and vision impairments. The press conference was organised by Sense International India, an organisation working for the uplift of deafblind persons. Spastics Society Coordinator Sanam Nair said, “When they undergo the process to obtain their disability certification, they are categorised under three different disabilities separately, and never together. This does not reflect on their Unique Disability ID Card either. If multiple disabilities with deafblindness are specified on their card, their individual needs could be addressed.” This, she points out, will lead to changes at the policy level. “This will help raise awareness and can lead to job opportunities for persons with deafblindness,” she added. 0ad0228b2f83465a.title: How AI is perfecting the art of government obfuscation
0ad0228b2f83465a.summary: Published - November 06, 2026 12:34 am IST ‘Nearly every other press note speaks of the unknown golden future under ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’. Phrases such as “digitally empowered society” and “knowledge economy” are liberally thrown around, along with the typical governance-speak: “holistic”, “convergence”, “capacity building”, “citizen-centric”, “grassroots” and so on’ | Photo Credit: viksitindia.com Jonathan Lynn and Antony Jay created the memorable fictional politician, The Right Hon. James Hacker. The two-part Yes Minister and Yes Prime Minister diaries of Hacker dealing with bureaucrats never gets old. I recently turned to them after frustrated encounters with government press notes packed with buzzwords that spoke a lot but said very little. In the editor’s note to the first volume, Hacker’s political training is blamed for him using “twenty words where one would do, to dictate millions of words where mere thousands would suffice, and to use language to blur and fudge issues and events so that they became incomprehensible to others.” These lines are a fitting description of government press notes that use various tools of evasion, serving to deliver two contradictory objectives: publicising the government’s achievements while concealing any information on shortcomings. This is an age-old trick that many governments have deployed. But today a new era of obfuscation is upon us, thanks to AI. 592fbd967218be3e.title: CM directs officials to begin Kaleshwaram barrage restoration works in December
592fbd967218be3e.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:32 am IST - HYDERABAD Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy with his Cabinet colleagues N. Uttam Kumar Reddy and Ponnam Prabhakar, at a meeting in Hyderabad on Thursday. Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy has directed officials to take up restoration of the damaged Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages of the Kaleshwaram project strictly in accordance with the recommendations of national-level experts and the National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA), with a target of commencing the works in December. At a review meeting here, the Chief Minister asked officials to secure the final approvals by the end of November. He also asked Ministers to counter the misleading propaganda that water available at Medigadda. It was also discussed in the Cabinet later. For water lifted from Medigadda to reach the Yellampalli reservoir, the gates of Annaram and Sundilla barrages would have to be closed. However, the NDSA had advised that the gates of these two barrages, which have structural defects, should remain open. On the utilisation of Godavari waters through alternative arrangements, Mr. Reddy said the government had lifted water on an unprecedented scale through the Devadula and Sitarama lift irrigation schemes to prevent the downstream Godavari water from going waste. While the previous government lifted an average of 9.57 tmc ft annually through Devadula, the average had increased to 18.13 tmc ft during the last three years, registering an increase of 89%. By October this year, 16.71 tmc ft had been lifted through Devadula and 8.10 tmc ft through Sitarama, taking the combined utilisation to 24.81 tmc ft, he said. The Odisha government had deployed 16 platoons of police and erected three border checkpoints, restricting people’s entry and exit. However, several voters sneaked out from the borders to cast votes. The Andhra Pradesh government had set up a polling booth for villagers of Kotia at Sariki in its State boundary. Similarly, Bhrugu Buxipatra, a senior BJD leader, said a few had crossed borders to vote. However, this time, the people of Odisha were successful by not letting Andhra Pradesh set up its polling booth inside Odisha, he said. In the run-up to elections, political parties from Odisha had camped at borders by not allowing polling booths inside the State. Both Odisha and Andhra Pradesh have been claiming their jurisdictional rights since 1950s. 3689fab72c5b5fde.title: Urvil warms up for Mushtaq Ali Trophy in style
3689fab72c5b5fde.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:51 am IST - Ahmedabad Urvil won the Player-of-the-Match award. | Photo Credit: M.R. Praveen Chandran Urvil Patel arguably made an early switch to white-ball mode ahead of the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (SMAT) as he blasted a whirlwind double century against Kerala in the Ranji Trophy at the Narendra Modi Stadium. The game-changing unbeaten 210 off just 227 balls was the cornerstone of Gujarat’s massive innings and 64-run win against Kerala and served as a perfect warm up for Urvil for the upcoming T20 tournament. Kerala never recovered from Urvil’s brutal assault. It was a definitive statement knock from Urvil, who previously had showcased his big-hitting prowess for Chennai Super Kings in the IPL. “It was my maiden double century in First Class cricket and I am happy that it came in a winning cause. I am always an aggressive batter and I love to play my strokes. When I came in we were in a spot of bother but I didn’t want the bowlers to dominate me, so I decided to attack. It was important to get a partnership going and Vishal (Jayswal) played beautifully,’’ he said. “Kerala spinners were getting into a fine rhythm so I decided to attack and I took my chances against Aditya Sarvate. To be honest we didn’t want to bat again on this pitch so we needed to post a big total and it was important for me to continue batting till the end. It is a good win for us. I hope to carry this form into SMAT and help my side win the tournament,’’ he added. f9fba18ba4b3a126.title: Hyderabad startup opens India’s first private space debris recovery facility
f9fba18ba4b3a126.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:30 am IST - HYDERABAD Hyderabad-based startup Cosmoserve Space on Thursday unveiled ‘Base 1’, touted as India’s first private facility and only the sixth in the world equipped with space-vision systems and microgravity simulation capabilities for satellite servicing and space debris recovery. The facility was inaugurated by Union Minister of State for Science & Technology and Space Dr. Jitendra Singh and Telangana IT and Industries Minister D. Sridhar Babu. Spread across multiple specialised laboratories, Base 1 combines satellite integration, space robotics, mission simulation and orbital capture technologies under one roof, enabling the company to design, build, test and operate satellite-servicing missions. It houses an Orbital Rendezvous and Capture Lab, a Space Robotics Innovation Lab, an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integration, and a Mission Simulation and Control Centre. Beyond recovering space debris, the centre will focus on in-orbit satellite repairs, refuelling and maintenance services. Congratulating the company, Dr. Jitendra Singh said the facility reflects the growing technological capabilities of India’s private space startups. Mr. Sridhar Babu said Hyderabad had emerged as a major spacetech hub, with more than 30 companies working on launch vehicles, space data centres, debris-removal systems and other advanced technologies. Cosmoserve founder and CEO Dr. Chiranjeevi Phanindra said the company aims to address one of the biggest challenges facing the global space industry: orbital debris. Of the nearly 28,000 satellites currently in orbit, about 10,000 are non-operational, while millions of debris fragments pose risks to active satellites and space missions. 78a6fb4fb90b2725.title: Linette banks on Chennai ‘memories’ to rediscover mojo
78a6fb4fb90b2725.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:27 am IST - CHENNAI Magda Linette. | Photo Credit: R. RAGU The last time Magda Linette was in Chennai, she was just months away from the best Grand Slam run of her career. After finishing runner-up at the WTA Chennai Open in 2022, she went on to reach her maiden Australian Open semifinals in January 2023. Now, back in the city amid a challenging season, the Polish player hopes “good memories” will help rediscover her rhythm. “I feel like I had a little bit worse time recently. And now I started getting my groove back (here), which is great. So yeah, definitely, it helps…brings back good memories,” said Linette after defeating Japan’s Moyuka Uchijima 7-6(5), 6-0 to move into the quarterfinals of the Chennai Open on Thursday. The 34-year-old has suffered seven first-round exits in the past five months. Rather than let the results dictate her approach, Linette chose to stay the course and work through the difficult phase. “I think it was a combination of things. A couple of (tough) draws, and then you lose a bit of your self-confidence and then you lose from edge points. And then just like that something spirals down. “It was important to keep working. Basically, you try your best not to panic and not find any excuses, which is not easy because you get a lot of criticism. And, it’s also not easy to go out there and try to work on things and fail and fail again. But I decided this year to go through with it. The ups and downs are necessary in sports,” said Linette. Through it all, she has had support in her corner, including Polish great Agnieszka Radwanska, who works with her as a consultant for 10-12 weeks a year. And, with her confidence slowly returning, Friday’s quarterfinal clash against Mai Hontama could help Linette script the start of her comeback. 0ac926e812a8efb6.title: Emami Q2 results: Profit rises nearly 2% at ₹145 cr, revenue up 36%
0ac926e812a8efb6.summary: Homegrown FMCG major Emami Ltd on Thursday reported a marginal decline of 1.92 per cent in its Profit After Tax at Rs 145.50 crore for September quarter FY27, on account of elevated input costs and normalisation of the effective tax rate. The company had posted a PAT of Rs 148.35 crore in the July-September period a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Kolkata-headquartered Emami. Revenue from operations was up 36.2 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,087.65 crore in the September quarter under review. "Input costs remained elevated through the quarter. However, EBITDA grew by 25 per cent to Rs 222 crore and profit before tax grew 29 per cent to Rs 194 crore. Profit after tax was lower largely due to the normalisation of the effective tax rate following the phase-out of fiscal benefits," said Emami in its earnings statement. Total expenses were at Rs 865.33 crore, up 39.57 per cent in the September quarter of FY27. In the quarter, Emami's domestic business grew by 49 per cent

d93d19dc3bb70bb4.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:19 am IST - VISAKHAPATNAM The Andhra Pradesh Pollution Control Board (APPCB) has stepped up measures to curb air and noise pollution across the State, directing district administrations and police, transport and municipal authorities to enforce environmental regulations and monitor pollution levels, particularly during Deepavali. In a recent communication to Collectors, Magistrates, Superintendents of Police, Municipal Commissioners and Police Commissioners of Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam, the Board called for joint inspection teams to prevent the sale, transportation and use of banned firecrackers. It also directed officials to monitor air quality and noise levels in all district headquarters and towns, following orders issued on October 16. The APPCB on Wednesday said its monitoring during Deepavali 2025 had recorded PM10 levels of up to 238 micrograms per cubic metre and PM2.5 levels of 138 micrograms per cubic metre in Visakhapatnam. Only green crackers approved by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI) will be permitted in cities and towns where air quality is moderate or better, subject to court directions. Conventional crackers containing banned chemicals, including barium salts, are prohibited. Permitted packs must carry unique QR codes linked to their registration, licence and test certificates, the Board said. The prescribed noise limits (in dB(A)) are 75 during the day and 70 at night in industrial areas; 65 and 55 in commercial areas; 55 and 45 in residential areas; and 50 and 40 in silence zones. Daytime is from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. and night-time from 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. Areas within 100 metres of hospitals, educational institutions and courts are designated silence zones, where honking is prohibited. 481be06aae8907b4.title: World Trade Center township on the anvil for Chengalpattu
481be06aae8907b4.summary: Updated - November 06, 2026 12:31 am IST - CHENNAI GTB Developers (GT Bharathi Urban Developers Pvt Ltd) announced that it has been granted a licence by the World Trade Centers Association (WTCA) to develop World Trade Center Chengalpattu. This particular project is planned as an IT integrated township of 100 to 150 acre, rather than an industrial estate. The project has an estimated value of ₹7,000 crore and will be developed in phases over approximately ten years. The proposed masterplan includes commercial and IT office space, hospitality, residences and an education zone. GTB is at an advanced stage of identifying and securing land for the project. GTB is also pursuing a second World Trade Center development in Kanchipuram district, proposed across approximately 500 acres. Unlike Chengalpattu, it is envisaged as an industrial World Trade Center, with manufacturing and data centre zones alongside infrastructure, education and hospitality. GTB intends to explore the project under a public-private partnership (PPP) model, one of the structures under which World Trade Centers are developed globally. flags: Contradictory claims: Summary states Herzog opens talks, but another line says he will announce decision on Sunday (implying talks haven't started or mandate not yet given).

Factually incorrect: In the 2019 Israeli election (which this appears to reference), Benny Gantz (Blue and White) won the mandate to form a government, not Benny Eisenkot (Yesh Atid). Eisenkot did not win 67 nods to be PM; Gantz's coalition had the majority.

Timeline inconsistency: Herzog typically gives the mandate to the leader of the largest party or a coalition with a majority. Eisenkot's party was not the largest, and no coalition led by him had 61 seats at the time of the initial mandate decision.
Source reliability: The source is a Google News RSS feed, which aggregates headlines from various outlets, leading to a jumbled and potentially contradictory summary.

3722fa8859ea88c9.title: Britannia Q2 net profit rises 10.8% to ₹726 crore on volume growth
3722fa8859ea88c9.summary: Bakery food company Britannia Industries Ltd on Thursday reported an increase of 10.82 per cent rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 725.99 crore for the September quarter of FY27, on a year-on-year basis, led by volume growth. The company had posted a net profit of Rs 655.06 crore in the July-September quarter a year ago, according to a regulatory filing from Britannia Industries. Britannia Industries' revenue from the sale of products was up 16.6 per cent to Rs 5,541.57 crore in the September quarter. The sales growth was "led by volume growth of 13 per cent", said Britannia Industries in its earnings statement. Its revenue from operations was up 15.64 per cent to Rs 5,597.79 crore in the second quarter of FY27. It was at Rs 4,840.63 crore in the corresponding quarter. Britannia's total expenses were at Rs 4,690.47 crore, up 17 per cent in Q2, FY27. Its total income, which includes other income, was up 15.9 per cent to Rs 5,671.30 crore in the September quarter. b9f1a3137bab4876.title: Chawri Bazar building collapse: CM orders inquiry, FIR against contractor
b9f1a3137bab4876.summary: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar, which claimed two lives and left four others injured, and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor. The chief minister also ordered the immediate suspension of the concerned junior engineer (JE) and assistant engineer (AE) in connection with the incident. She directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and provide immediate ex-gratia assistance to the affected families. "Stringent action will be taken against those found responsible, in accordance with the law," the chief minister said. The building collapsed around 9.50 am in Gali Sitara, near the Chawri Bazar Metro station, police said. b9f1a3137bab4876.headline_en: Chawri Bazar building collapse: CM orders inquiry, FIR against contractor
b9f1a3137bab4876.raw_facts: Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta on Thursday ordered an inquiry into the collapse of a three-storey building under construction in Old Delhi's Chawri Bazar, which claimed two lives and left four others injured, and directed the registration of an FIR against the contractor. The chief minister also ordered the immediate suspension of the concerned junior engineer (JE) and assistant engineer (AE) in connection with the incident. She directed officials to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured and provide immediate ex-gratia assistance to the affected families. "Stringent action will be taken against those found responsible, in accordance with the law," the chief minister said. The building collapsed around 9.50 am in Gali Sitara, near the Chawri Bazar Metro station, police said. Two bodies were pulled out from the debris by a Delhi Fire Services (DFS) rescue team, while four injured people were taken to a hospital by locals before the fire department teams arrive
